items.title: One Embedding Doesn't Fit All: Rethinking Speaker Modeling Robustness Across Speaker-Centric Tasks
items.abstract: Speaker embeddings have become a fundamental representation for a wide range of speaker-centric speech applications, including speaker verification, diarization, target speaker extraction, and personalized speech interaction. However, a speaker representation optimized for one task or acoustic condition does not necessarily generalize well to others. This survey revisits the notion of robustness in speaker modeling from a broader, task-oriented perspective. We review recent progress in learning speaker representations under variations in acoustics, speech content, duration, and domain, and discuss how speaker information is exploited differently across downstream tasks. Particular attention is given to the trade-offs between task-independent speaker representations and task-adaptive modeling. Finally, we highlight emerging challenges and opportunities toward more generalizable, transferable, and task-aware speaker modeling for future speech and multimodal systems.

items.title: SDR-LLM: Speech-LLM Based End-to-End Speaker Diarization and Recognition with Sentence-Level Temporal Modeling
items.authors: Renjie Yu(Tsinghua University); Yixuan Zhou(Tsinghua University); Shun Lei(Tsinghua University); Xiang Li(Tsinghua University); Runchuan Ye(Tsinghua University); Yikai Huang(ModelBest Inc.); Guoyang Zeng(Tsinghua University); Zhiyong Wu(Tsinghua University)
items.abstract: Speaker Diarization and Recognition (SDR) is crucial for multi-speaker audio. Cascaded systems suffer from error accumulation, while many end-to-end (E2E) models fail to provide fine-grained temporal alignment. We propose a unified Speech-LLM framework that predicts speaker identities, text, and millisecond-level timestamps. Our method introduces a FIFO output sequence, integrating voiceprint IDs and temporal boundaries into autoregressive generation. Training high-accuracy E2E SDR models requires large amounts of annotated data, which is scarce. To address this, we use a two-stage approach: first, simulating speaker turns and timing with synthetic data, followed by fine-tuning with a small amount of real-world data. Experiments on AISHELL-4, AliMeeting, and OleSpeech show that our approach outperforms E2E models in transcription accuracy and achieves diarization comparable to cascaded systems. Our method balances transcription precision and temporal alignment in real-world corpus.

items.title: Where Do Backdoors Live? A Component-Level Analysis of Backdoor Propagation in Speech Language Models
items.authors: Alexandrine Fortier(University of British Columbia); Thomas Thebaud(Johns Hopkins University); Jesus Villalba(Johns Hopkins University); Najim Dehak(Johns Hopkins University); Patrick Cardinal(École de technologie supérieure); Peter West(University of British Columbia)
items.abstract: Speech language models (SLMs) are systems of systems: independent components that unite to achieve a common goal. Despite their heterogeneous nature, SLMs are often studied end-to-end; how information flows through the pipeline remains obscure. We investigate this question through the lens of backdoor attacks. We first establish that backdoors can propagate through the SLM, leaving all tasks highly vulnerable. From this, we design a component analysis to discover the role each component takes in backdoor learning. We find that backdoor persistence or erasure is highly dependent on the targeted component. Beyond propagation, we examine how backdoors are encoded in shared multitask embeddings, showing that poisoned samples are not directly separable from benign ones, challenging a common separability assumption used in filtering defenses. Our findings emphasize the need to treat multimodal pipelines as intricate systems with unique vulnerabilities, not solely extensions of unimodal ones.

items.title: Tight Boundary Prediction in Speaker Diarization Using Causal-Anticausal Consistency
items.authors: Shota Horiguchi(NTT, Inc.); Marc Delcroix(NTT, Inc.); Naohiro Tawara(NTT, Inc.); Takanori Ashihara(NTT, Inc.); Atsushi Ando(NTT, Inc.)
items.abstract: Multi-talker conversational automatic speech recognition data are often used to train speaker diarization models. Because such data prioritize semantic continuity, pauses and boundary margins are included within speech segments, resulting in loose annotations. Models trained on such data tend to internalize mechanisms that reproduce this looseness, although tight speech intervals are sometimes preferable for downstream applications. In this paper, we address the novel task of enabling models to produce tight predictions using loose labels. Our method generates tighter pseudo labels using causal and anticausal models, which are inherently incapable of learning loosening behavior. We further propose a co-training scheme that iteratively tightens labels and updates both models for more progressive refinement. Experimental results show that the proposed method recovers about 70 % of the tightening effect achieved by ideal tight-label training and improves downstream performance.

items.title: Modeling Overlapped Speech with Shuffles
items.authors: Matthew Wiesner(Johns Hopkins University; LISN, CNRS); Samuele Cornell(Carnegie Mellon University); Alexander Polok(Brno University of Technology); Lucas Ondel-Yang(LISN, CNRS); Lukáš Burget(Brno University of Technology); Sanjeev Khudanpur(Johns Hopkins University)
items.abstract: We propose to model parallel streams of data, such as overlapped speech, using shuffles. Specifically, this paper shows how the shuffle product and partial order finite-state automata (FSAs) can be used for alignment and speaker-attributed transcription of overlapped speech. We train using the total score on these FSAs as a loss function, marginalizing over all possible serializations of overlapping sequences at subword, word, and phrase levels. To reduce graph size, we impose temporal constraints by constructing partial order FSAs. We address speaker attribution by modeling (token, speaker) tuples directly. Viterbi alignment through the shuffle product FSA directly enables one-pass alignment. We evaluate performance on synthetic LibriSpeech overlaps. To our knowledge, this is the first algorithm that enables single-pass alignment of multi-talker recordings. All algorithms are implemented using k2 / Icefall.

items.title: ProSarc: Prosody-Aware Sarcasm Recognition Framework via Temporal Prosodic Incongruity
items.authors: Prathamjyot Singh(Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology); Ashima Sood(Ulster University); Sahil Sharma(Ulster University); Jasmeet Singh(Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology)
items.abstract: We present ProSarc, an audio-only framework that detects sarcasm by modelling temporal prosodic incongruity, that is, the mismatch between local prosodic dynamics and the utterance-level emotional baseline. Dual encoding paths, a Global Emotion Encoder and a Temporal Prosody Encoder (BiLSTM + multi-head attention), feed a Prosodic Incongruity Analyzer that produces a scalar incongruity score for classification. Monte Carlo dropout provides uncertainty estimates, and an attention-based mechanism localises sarcastic onset without frame-level labels. ProSarc outperforms prior audio-only methods on MUStARD++ (F1 = 75.3) and generalises to spontaneous (PodSarc, F1 = 62.9) and cross-lingual speech (MuSaG, F1 = 65.6). Ten-run validation confirms the contribution of incongruity modelling (Wilcoxon p=0.002, Cohen's d=1.51). Human evaluation shows that model uncertainty tracks perceptual ambiguity and predicted onsets align with human-annotated temporal windows.

items.title: A Two-Stage Defence for Robust Federated Speech Emotion Recognition
items.authors: Yi Chang(Imperial College London); Sofiane Laridi(Leibniz University Hannover); Zhao Ren(University of Bremen); Gregory Palmer(Leibniz University Hannover); Björn W. Schuller(Imperial College London); Marco Fisichella(Leibniz University Hannover)
items.abstract: With machine learning and speech processing advancements, speech emotion recognition has gained popularity recently. However, speech data cannot be protected when it is uploaded and processed on servers in the internet-of-things applications of speech emotion recognition. Further, deep neural networks have proven to be vulnerable to human-indistinguishable adversarial perturbations. The adversarial attacks generated from the perturbations may result in deep neural networks wrongly predicting the emotional states. We propose a novel federated adversarial learning framework for protecting both data and deep neural networks. The proposed framework consists of i) federated learning for data privacy, and ii) adversarial training at the training stage and randomisation at the testing stage for model robustness. The experiments show our proposed framework effectively protects speech data locally and improve model robustness against a series of adversarial attacks.

items.title: Segregate, Refine, Integrate: Decomposing Multimodal Fusion for Sentiment Analysis
items.authors: Alexios Filippakopoulos(National Technical University of Athens; Synaptic Bloom); Elias Kallioras(National Technical University of Athens); Nikolaos Xiros(National Technical University of Athens; Athena Research Center); Efthymios Georgiou(National Technical University of Athens; University of Bern); Alexandros Potamianos(National Technical University of Athens; Archimedes AI; Synaptic Bloom)
items.abstract: Multimodal fusion must simultaneously refine modality-specific signals and model cross-modal interactions; two competing objectives typically entangled within the same operation. We propose SeRIn (Segregate, Refine, Integrate), a multimodal LM fusion scheme that enforces this separation as an architectural prior. Modality-specific representations evolve along isolated pathways, each refined against its respective encoder context, while a dedicated cross-modal pathway accumulates their joint evolution without contaminating unimodal streams. Full cross-modal interaction is deferred to a final prediction step — ablations confirm that structured interactions, not added capacity, drive the gains; gate analysis under visual corruption reveals emergent modality reweighting without explicit supervision. SeRIn achieves state-of-the-art results on CH-SIMS and CMU-MOSEI, improving all metrics on both benchmarks.

items.title: An Acoustic Landmark Database of the English Lexicon via Articulatory Synthesis
items.authors: Mateo Cámara(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid; MIT); José Luis Blanco(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid); Juan Ignacio Godino-Llorente(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid); Jeung-Yoon Choi(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid); Stefanie Shattuck-Hufnagel(MIT)
items.abstract: Acoustic landmark theory treats speech as organized around the acoustic consequences of articulatory gestures that shape the vocal tract and airflow. Progress is limited by the scarcity of large, unambiguously annotated landmark datasets. We invert the problem by generating speech from landmark patterns. Using the Pink Trombone physical vocal-tract synthesizer, we produce an English lexicon for two adult configurations (male, female). With direct control of gestures, we place landmark labels algorithmically at the exact times of their physical events (e.g., oral closures/releases). The corpus contains >200,000 synthesized words, rendered for both configurations with time-aligned annotations; intelligibility is measured with STOI. We leverage it for statistics across the lexicon from an articulatory-event view, reporting landmark frequencies and dominant cue patterns, and enabling quantitative studies plus training/benchmarking of automatic landmark detectors.

items.title: NewAppVoice: Tools for Visualizing and Correcting Acoustic Measures
items.authors: Amélie Elmerich(CNRS & Sorbonne Nouvelle); Yao Dong(CNRS); Louise McKeever(CNRS & Sorbonne Nouvelle); Katia Chirkova(CNRS); Lise Crevier-Buchman(CNRS & Sorbonne Nouvelle; Université Paris Saclay); Claire Pillot-Loiseau(CNRS & Sorbonne Nouvelle); Angelique Amelot(CNRS & Sorbonne Nouvelle)
items.abstract: Phonetic analysis of little-studied languages, particularly those with complex segmental inventories or typologically rare features, often requires extensive manual verification of acoustic measurements. In the absence of established reference formant values, automatic extraction frequently produces systematic errors that must be visually inspected and corrected. Most large-scale scripts process datasets without interactive feedback, limiting transparency and reproducibility when manual intervention is necessary. This study presents NewAppVoice, a reproducible workflow integrating multiple formant-calculation algorithms with synchronized visualization of signals and measurements. Unlike fully automated pipelines, the software combines algorithmic processing with structured manual verification, improving reliability while ensuring transparency. The software and derived applications are freely available as open access tools supporting reproducible research on under-documented languages.

items.title: Beyond Residual Connections: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections for Robust Speaker Representation Learning
items.authors: Zezhong Jin(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Xiaoyu Wang(Baidu); Zhe Li(Hong Kong University); Chong-Xin Gan(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Zilong Huang(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Man-Wai Mak(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Kong Aik Lee(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)
items.abstract: Residual connections are fundamental to deep speaker recognition models, such as ECAPA-TDNN and ResNet. However, standard identity mapping limits information flow to a single path, constraining representation capacity. We introduce Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), reformulating residual paths as a multi-stream evolution where information is mixed through a doubly stochastic matrix. By employing Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations, mHC ensures energy conservation by preserving signal intensity and feature mean, which stabilizes gradients and mitigates signal degradation in complex networks. We evaluate mHC by replacing standard residual connections in backbones including ECAPA-TDNN, ResNet-34, Res2Net, and E-Res2Net. Extensive experiments on VoxCeleb1 demonstrate that mHC connections consistently enhances performance across all architectures, highlighting its effectiveness for robust speaker representation learning.

items.title: Mitigating Pruning-Quantization Compound Errors for Ultra-Lightweight ResNet34-Based Speaker Recognition
items.abstract: While deep neural networks (DNNs) have greatly advanced speaker recognition, backbone models such as ResNet34 still suffer from computation and memory footprints, making difficult to deploy on resource-constrained devices. To this end, we explored pruning and quantization techniques to compress speaker recognition model. Specifically, we propose a unified compression framework that combines channel pruning and low-bit quantization. Specifically, we propose ResRep-MB, a pruning strategy with multi-branch compactors for accurate channel importance assessment, achieving near-lossless structural compression. To mitigate the compound errors caused by pruning and INT4 quantization, we propose Progressive Pruning-Quantization Distillation (PPQD), which employs a dual-teacher mechanism. Experiments on VoxCeleb1 and CN-Celeb1 demonstrate that the compressed ResNet34 achieves a 19.2× compression ratio with only a 6.8% relative EER degradation, while maintaining robust cross-language performance.

items.title: Continuous 2D Spectral—Temporal Transformer for Speaker Verification
items.authors: Seongwook Ham(Soongsil University); Thien-Phuc Doan(Soongsil University)
items.abstract: Recent speaker verification (SV) systems often employ hybrid architectures that combine spectral—temporal modeling with temporal aggregation. However, approaches such as ReDimNet perform global dependency modeling after collapsing the spectral—temporal grid into a temporal representation, which removes the explicit spectral-temporal structure. We propose Continuous 2D Spectral-Temporal Transformer (C2D-ST), which maintains the spectral—temporal representation throughout the backbone and performs global dependency modeling directly on the spectral—temporal grid, with temporal-only modeling applied only in a final stage. Experiments on VoxCeleb show that C2D-ST achieves competitive performance with strong parameter efficiency, reaching 0.507 average EER with 6.9M parameters.

items.title: A Federated Learning-Based Speaker Recognition Method with Dual Classification Heads
items.authors: Ying Meng(Xinjiang University); Zhihua Fang(Xinjiang University; AGIBOT); Liang He(Xinjiang University; Tsinghua University)
items.abstract: In speaker recognition tasks, acquiring data requires significant technical and financial resources for individual organizations, while also posing risks of privacy breaches. Applying federated learning architectures can address these issues, but model performance may degrade when confronting data heterogeneity challenges. In this paper, we propose a federated learning-based speaker recognition method with dual classification heads. By introducing a more knowledgeable classification head, local models can acquire more comprehensive global knowledge, thereby improving model performance. Our method achieved an average EER improvement of 46.5% over local training and 7.6% over FedAvg when trained on the VoxCeleb2 dataset. When jointly trained on the VoxCeleb and CN-Celeb datasets, the average EER improved by 68.8% over local training and 5.4% over FedAvg.

items.title: Learning Global Key Knowledge for Federated Speaker Recognition via Fisher Information
items.authors: Ying Meng(Xinjiang University); Zhihua Fang(Xinjiang University; AGIBOT); Liang He(Xinjiang University; Tsinghua University)
items.abstract: Speaker recognition relies on substantial data to enhance model performance, but the large-scale transmission of data by individual organizations incurs privacy and economic costs. Federated learning addresses privacy concerns by avoiding direct data transmission. However, due to inconsistent client data distributions, local models may learn redundant knowledge, leading to degraded performance. In this work, we utilise the Fisher Information Matrix to extract key dimensions from embeddings, enabling representation alignment between global and local models. By instructing local models to learn critical knowledge from the global model, we mitigate the detrimental effects of redundant knowledge, thereby enhancing overall model performance.

items.title: HistoMatch: Unified Transient-Steady Assessment for Noise-Robust Semi-Supervised Speaker Verification
items.authors: Shenghan Gao(UCAS; IOA); Xueshuai Zhang(IOA); Pengyuan Zhang(UCAS; IOA); Yonghong Yan(UCAS; IOA)
items.abstract: Speaker verification systems have gained widespread applications across various domains, benefiting from advances in deep learning. However, acquiring large-scale labeled data remains challenging, making semi-supervised learning with pseudo-labeling a critical research focus. Current pseudo-labeling approaches predominantly rely on confidence thresholds-a transient metric vulnerable to distortions induced by random segmentation and noise augmentation. To overcome this limitation, we propose HistoMatch, a novel mechanism that leverages historical prediction stability as a steady-state metric. Combined with transient confidence, it forms a Dual-state History-based Stability Evaluator (DHSE) for high-quality unlabeled data selection. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our semi-supervised approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on all three VoxCeleb1 test sets, with remarkable equal error rates (EER) of 0.91%, 1.13%, and 2.13%-closely approaching fully supervised benchmarks.

items.title: Self-supervised Speaker Verification with High-Confidence Pseudo-Label Selection and DINO-Style Self-Distillation Based on Pre-trained Models
items.authors: Yishuang Li(Malanshan audio & video Lab); Yi Yu(Malanshan audio & video Lab); Wanli Dong(Malanshan audio & video Lab); Weihao Gan(Malanshan audio & video Lab)
items.abstract: In this paper, we propose a self-supervised speaker verification (SS-SV) method based on pre-trained models (PTMs), which improves performance via high-confidence pseudo-label selection and DINO-style self-distillation. We select the top-K most speaker-discriminative Transformer layers from PTMs and cluster their representations separately to generate multiple pseudo-label sets. Using label alignment, we retain samples with consistent clustering as high-confidence pseudo-labeled data, while others are treated as unlabeled. We perform pseudo-supervised learning with label noise correction loss on the high-confidence set;for unlabeled data we use an EMA teacher to provide soft distillation targets and apply a consistency loss for regularization. These objectives are jointly optimized to train the SV model. Experiments on the VoxCeleb dataset show that our SS-SV method achieves performance comparable to current state-of-the-art approaches, demonstrating its effectiveness.

items.title: Stabilizing Short Duration Speaker Verification through Neural Re-scoring with Hybrid Enrollment
items.authors: Zhiqi Ai(Shanghai University); Cheng Han(Shanghai University); Shiyi Mu(Shanghai University); Zhiyong Chen(Hithink RoyalFlush AI Research Institute); Yongjin Zhou(Shanghai University); Shugong Xu(Xi’an Jiaotong Liverpool University)
items.abstract: Short-duration speaker verification (SDSV) is crucial for personalized keyword spotting, where test utterances are typically shorter than three seconds. Limited speech duration results in unstable speaker representations and increased sensitivity to noise and phoneme variations, thereby degrading performance. To investigate this issue, we construct VoxPhrase, a large-scale SDSV corpus automatically segmented from the VoxCeleb dataset. Our analysis shows that text-dependent (TD) enrollment is constrained by duration and yields unstable speaker representations. In contrast, although text-independent (TI) enrollment introduces content mismatch, its representations become more stable as the enrollment duration increases. Accordingly, we propose a hybrid-enrollment neural re-scoring framework that combines TD and TI enrollment and performs frame-level comparison via parallel cross-attention. Experiments on VoxPhrase demonstrate consistent improvements across multiple speaker models.

items.title: VieSpeaker: A Large-Scale Vietnamese Speaker Recognition Dataset Beyond Visual Dependency
items.authors: Viet Hoang Pham(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Tran Trung Nguyen(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Bao Thu Ho(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Phuong Tuan Dat(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Thi Thu Trang Nguyen(Hanoi University of Science and Technology)
items.abstract: Speaker recognition has advanced rapidly with large-scale training datasets, yet Vietnamese remains under-resourced, with existing corpora limited in scale and acoustic diversity. Most large-scale datasets rely on facial cues to link speech with speaker identities, restricting data collection to recordings where speakers appear on camera. We propose a face-independent dataset construction pipeline and introduce VieSpeaker, a large-scale Vietnamese speaker recognition dataset. Our approach leverages textual metadata and large language model reasoning to infer speaker identities from transcripts and contextual information. VieSpeaker contains approximately 902 hours of speech from 4,715 speakers. Experiments show that models trained on VieSpeaker achieve improved robustness and generalization compared to existing Vietnamese datasets. This work demonstrates the feasibility of face-independent dataset construction and provides a new direction for building large-scale speech resources.

items.title: Confusion-Transport Pruning: Optimal-Transport Redundancy and CKA Geometry Distillation for Hard-Set Robust Speaker Verification
Function words: a topic independent approach to word n-gram selection for forensic speaker comparison
items.authors: Michael Carne(Australian National University)
items.abstract: This paper highlights an issue with likelihood ratio-based forensic speaker comparison (LR-based FSC) systems that exploit speaker idiosyncrasies in word choice. A baseline experiment using word n-gram features from speech transcripts of 104 Australian male speakers achieves a Cllr of 0.60. However, it is shown that topic dependent terms are included in the feature set, which may bias the result. In turn, this may lead to an overestimation of the strength of evidence obtainable from word n-gram based features. A simple but novel approach to circumventing this problem using function words is presented and evaluated. An explicitly defined features set of 156 function words is shown to yield a Cllr of 0.83. Subsequent evaluation of five filter based feature selection methods applied to the set demonstrates an notable improvement in performance when using the ANOVA F-ratio procedure (Cllr = 0.78). This result is coupled with a substantial reduction in dimension size to k= 50 features.

items.title: Codec-induced Mismatch, Speech Duration, and Speaker-dependent Effect in a DNN-based Forensic Speaker Recognition System
items.authors: Guangmou Deng(Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Bruce Xiao Wang(Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Vincent Hughes(University of York)
items.abstract: The performance of forensic automatic speaker recognition (FASR) systems under the combined effects of codec-induced mismatch and different questioned-speech (QS) durations remains insufficiently understood, particularly at the individual speaker level. This study investigates the combined impact of representative lossy speech codecs (G.711 A-law, AMR-NB, and Opus) and QS duration on a DNN (ResNet34-MHA)-based FASR system. System-level performance was generally good across all codec conditions, especially with >30s speech. Codec effects vary, however, with low-bitrate AMR-NB causing the greatest degradation in performance and Opus having minimal impact. Crucially, individual-level analyses reveal substantial speaker-dependent variability that is obscured by system-level metrics: some speakers exhibit persistently poor or unstable performance, and speakers with poorer overall performance are more sensitive to codec-induced mismatch. These findings demonstrate that promising system-level performance does not guarantee good performance for all speakers and highlights the need for individual-level analysis when testing DNN-based FASR systems.

items.title: Addressing random spatial translations in measured microphone directional responses by maximizing finite order energy
items.authors: Xue Wen(Samsung)
items.abstract: Directional responses measured on real-world devices are disturbed by unknown translations in space, which add uncertainty to spatial signal processing methods that use such data. In this paper we propose the concept of finite order centroid, which is the translation that maximizes directional response energy in finite order spatial harmonics. The centroid is calculated from the measured response as a second translation, to the effect that it cancels any random perturbation to the first. This leads to a calibrated directional response that is free from said positioning uncertainty, and has spatio-acoustical guarantees useful for downstream processing. We use several simple tasks to show the use of finite order centroids in spatial signal processing.

items.title: Blind Room Impulse Response Identification via Reverberant Speech Spectrum Reconstruction
items.authors: Pengyu Wang(Zhejiang University; Westlake University); Xiaofei Li(Westlake University; Westlake Institute for Advanced Study)
items.abstract: This paper proposes Rec-RIR for blind room impulse response (RIR) identification. Based on the convolutive transfer function (CTF) approximation, we propose a multi-task deep neural network, which sequentially removes noise and reverberation from speech recording, and estimates the CTF filter by reverberant speech spectrum reconstruction. Subsequently, a pseudo intrusive measurement process is employed to convert the CTF filter into RIR by simulating a common intrusive RIR measurement procedure. Experimental results demonstrate that Rec-RIR achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in blind RIR identification.

items.title: Sensitivity Analysis of Generative Spatial Audio Metrics : A Study on Responsiveness, Smoothness, and Symmetry
items.authors: Purnima Kamath(New York University); Adrian Roman(New York University); Koichi Saito(Sony AI); Yuki Mitsufuji(Sony AI; Sony Group Corporation; New York University); Juan Bello(New York University)
items.abstract: Evaluating generative spatial audio for First-Order Ambisonics (FOA) remains challenging due to a limited understanding of how metrics respond to changes in spatial parameters such as azimuth and elevation. We propose a framework to analyze metric sensitivity along continuous spatial trajectories, drawing on principles of sensitivity analysis in parametric sound synthesis. Using controlled FOA scenes with increasing scene complexity, we define three desiderata for metric behavior: Responsiveness, Smoothness, and Symmetry. We assess standard distribution-based and sample-based metrics, including Fréchet Audio Distance (FAD), intensity vectors, and acoustic maps. Our findings show that FAD using localization-specific embeddings and acoustic maps yield high Responsiveness and robust Smoothness and Symmetry across conditions, while intensity vectors degrade with increasing scene complexity. This is the first step towards investigating the sensitivity of metrics for generative spatial audio.

items.title: FoleyImmersive: Decoupling What and Where for Video-to-First-Order Ambisonics
items.authors: Liming Liang(Peking University); Lingfeng Yang(South China University of Technology); Luo Chen(Peking University); Chenxing Li(Tencent AI Lab); Yuexian Zou(Peking University)
items.abstract: We study immersive video-to-audio (V2A) by generating first-order ambisonics (FOA) from silent field-of-view (FoV) videos. Challenges include sparse semantics in video-FOA corpora and content-geometry entanglement: end-to-end models blur "what" and "where", while two-stage pipelines trade semantic fidelity for spatial coherence. We present FoleyImmersive and a semantics-augmented dataset, YT-AmbiSem, which augments YT-Ambigen with structured descriptions from Qwen2.5-VL-7B. Stage 1 (WHAT) uses a semantics-first diffusion model with multi-rate cross-frame attention and probabilistic time modulation to generate mono W. Stage 2 (WHERE) spatializes W to XYZ via a complex-STFT U-Net conditioned on per-frame visuals and camera direction; a lightweight directional residual mixer applies view-dependent bottleneck gating to stabilize localization with minimal content drift. We achieve state-of-the-art semantic and spatial metrics. Demo and dataset are available.

items.title: Learning Self-Supervised Spatial Representations via Soft Acoustic Contrastive Alignment
items.authors: Yotam Silverman(Tel Aviv University); Bracha Laufer-Goldshtein(Tel Aviv University)
items.abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for improving downstream performance when annotated data is limited. However, most existing audio SSL methods process single-channel inputs and focus on learning spectral representations, which are often insufficient for spatially sensitive tasks like direction-of-arrival or reverberation estimation. In this work, we propose a self-supervised framework for binaural audio that integrates spatial priors directly into the pre-training objective. We introduce the Soft Acoustic Contrastive (SAC) loss, a geometric objective that structures the latent space by aligning embeddings based on shared acoustic properties, such as directionality and diffuseness, without requiring ground-truth labels. Experimental results demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms baselines across five downstream spatial parameter estimation tasks.

items.title: Geometrically Constrained Decentralized Independent Vector Analysis for Distributed Microphone Arrays
items.authors: Changda Chen(Waseda University; Nanjing University); Yichen Yang(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Wei Liu(Waseda University; Wuhan University); Bing Zhu(Northwestern Polytechnical University); Gongping Huang(Wuhan University); Shoji Makino(Waseda University); Shuai Wang(Nanjing University)
items.abstract: This paper proposes a geometrically constrained decentral-ized independent vector analysis (GC-Dec-IVA) method for distributed microphone arrays. Recently proposed Dec-IVA method enables source separation by exchanging only power-related statistics to exploit cross-array information. However, this initial attempt often provides negligible improvement over applying IVA locally at each array, mainly due to the potential permutation inconsistency among arrays and the strong cross-array dependency implied by its source model. To address these limitations, we incorporate direction-of-arrival (DOA) information to derive GC-Dec-IVA, which mitigates permutation mismatch across arrays and enhances source alignment. Furthermore, a new source model is introduced to weaken cross-array dependency, improving robustness against permutation inconsistency in noisy environments. Experiments show the proposed method improves both the separation performance and cross-array permutation consistency.

items.title: Optimal Source Placement for TDoA-based Geometry Calibration of Distributed Microphone Arrays
items.authors: Xu Wang(Inner Mongolia University); Qintuya Si(Inner Mongolia University); Qingyin Zhao(Inner Mongolia University); De Hu(Inner Mongolia University)
items.abstract: Distributed microphone arrays (DMAs) are widely used in various audio/speech processing applications. As these applications require the geometric structure of the DMA as a priori knowledge, geometry calibration of DMAs is indispensable. However, most existing methods use randomly placed calibration sources, which may lead to a relatively higher Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB). In this paper, we use a mobile robot to act as the multiple calibration sources, and optimize its positions to expect an improved self-localization accuracy. Specifically, we derive the CRLB using time-difference-of-arrival measurements with time offsets. Then, the optimal robot's positions are obtained by minimizing the CRLB while constraining the robot positions within a restricted room. Additionally, we also present a multi-stage solution for scenarios with limited computational resources or demanding runtime requirements. Numerical experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed placement methods.

items.title: G2C-NET: A Grid-to-Continuous Neural Network for Sound Source Localization in Distributed Microphone Arrays
items.authors: Zhiyuan Yue(Inner Mongolia University); De Hu(Inner Mongolia University)
items.abstract: Grid-based sound source localization (SSL) has gained increasing attention in distributed microphone arrays as it reformulates the inherently nonconvex regression problem into a tractable classification task. However, the trade-off between grid resolution and computational complexity poses a fundamental challenge. To this end, we propose G2C-NET, a grid-to-continuous neural network which consists of two main modules: Global Likelihood Estimation (GLE) and Continuous Position Estimation (CPE). In the GLE module, we construct an adaptive pairwise feature aggregator to fuse the acoustic features from microphone pairs, generating the global likelihood distribution of source over grids. Then, the CPE module derives continuous source position via a weighted sum of high-confidence grids. Compared with existing grid-based SSL methods, G2C-NET achieves better performance at equivalent grid resolution. Experimental results validate its effectiveness.

items.title: Fast Multichannel Nonnegative Matrix Factorization with Directivity Regularization for DOA-Informed Speech Separation
items.authors: Ryosuke Ono(Kyoto University; RIKEN); Aditya Arie Nugraha(RIKEN); Yoshiaki Bando(AIST; RIKEN); Kazuyoshi Yoshii(Kyoto University; RIKEN)
items.abstract: This paper addresses DOA-informed multichannel speech separation under overdetermined conditions, where the number of speakers does not exceed the number of microphones. We focus on FastMNMF, a BSS method robust to unknown acoustic environments. Since FastMNMF represents real-source spatial covariance matrices in a jointly diagonalized domain, its diagonal components correspond to virtual spatial components rather than the real sources themselves. We propose directivity-regularized FastMNMF, which encourages each pseudo-separation filter to pass signals from the target speaker direction and suppress those from other speaker directions while tolerating DOA errors. The separation matrix is updated using a closed-form VCD-based rule. Experiments with simulated noisy simultaneous speech mixtures show that the proposed regularization improves separation performance.

items.title: SpkGuideDOA: Speaker-wise Representation Guidance for Multiple Moving Speaker Localization
items.authors: Yongseok Choi(Hanyang University); Davin Kim(Hanyang University); Joon-Hyuk Chang(Hanyang University)
items.abstract: Localizing multiple moving speakers in dynamic acoustic environments requires resolving time-varying spatial cues under severe spatial-spectral overlap. To address this challenge, we propose SpkGuideDOA, a framework that enhances a spatial cue estimator with speaker-wise representation guidance while maintaining computational efficiency. An auxiliary guidance generator extracts implicit speaker representations from multi-channel magnitudes and injects them via residual modulation at a pooled resolution. Training is driven by a localization objective with an additional loss that stabilizes the guidance branch. Joint permutation-invariant training ensures consistent speaker assignment across modules. Experiments on simulated mixtures and the LOCATA dataset demonstrate improved localization performance while maintaining computational efficiency.

items.title: Quantifying the Uncertainty of Blindly Estimated Room Embeddings Using a Dispersion-Calibrated Score
items.authors: Yang Xiang(University of Surrey); Philipp Götz(International Audio Laboratories Erlangen); Emanuël A. P. Habets(International Audio Laboratories Erlangen); Andreas Walther(Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits IIS); Wenwu Wang(University of Surrey); Philip J. B. Jackson(University of Surrey)
items.abstract: Room embeddings derived from reverberant speech are often unreliable: speech content and recording degradation can alter the representation even when speaker, room, and source-receiver geometry remain unchanged, degrading downstream task performance. We propose a framework that learns room embeddings robust to speech-content variation and a representation-level uncertainty score from reverberant speech without downstream-task supervision. The embedding is anchored to a structured room impulse response (RIR) latent space and trained using a multi-view data structure with KullbackLeibler (KL)-based alignment; a multi-positive contrastive term further refines robustness. A lightweight uncertainty head is calibrated using the dispersion of corruption-induced embeddings and optimized with a rank-based objective. Across waveform- and spectrogram-level corruptions, the score is consistent with representation dispersion and enables effective selective prediction while requiring only a single utterance at inference.

title: Multi-Channel Processing and Specialized Acquisition (UAV, Radar, Hearables)

items.title: CAPS: A Cascaded Reconstruction Model to Power Saving in Hearables Using Sub-Nyquist Sampling with Bandwidth Extension
items.authors: Tarikul Islam(George Mason University); Sajid F. Dipto(George Mason University); Luke B. Baja-Ricketts(George Mason University); David C. Vergano(George Mason University); Anomadarshi Barua(George Mason University)
items.abstract: Hearables are wearable computers worn on the ear. Bone conduction microphones are used with air conduction microphones in hearables for multimodal speech enhancement in noisy conditions. Despite this potential, current models largely fail to explore how jointly reducing sampling bit resolution and sampling frequency in analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) of hearables impacts both power usage and audio quality. Furthermore, current frameworks cannot do sub-Nyquist sampling in hearables because they lack a method to reconstruct wideband signals from narrowband components. We therefore propose CAPS, which (i) intentionally employs sub-Nyquist sampling and low bit resolution in ADCs, achieving a 3.3x reduction in power consumption in hearables, and (ii) supports streaming operation on mobile platforms with an inference time of 1.36ms and a memory footprint of 11.04MB. CAPS ensures robust speech intelligibility in real-world settings, bridging the gap between efficiency and power savings.

items.title: An Investigation on Combining Geometry and Consistency Constraints into Phase Estimation for Speech Enhancement
items.authors: Chun-Wei Ho(Georgia Institute of Technology); Pin-Jui Ku(Georgia Institute of Technology; NVIDIA); Hao Yen(Georgia Institute of Technology; Microsoft); Sabato Marco Siniscalchi(Universit`a degli Studi di Palermo); Yu Tsao(Academia Sinica); Chin-Hui Lee(Georgia Institute of Technology)
items.abstract: We propose a novel iterative phase estimation framework, termed the multi-source Griffin-Lim algorithm (MSGLA), for speech enhancement under additive noise. The key idea is to exploit the consistency constraint of complex short-time Fourier transform (STFT) spectrograms to resolve the sign ambiguity inherent in geometry-based phase estimation. We further introduce a geometric formulation based on the law of sines and cosines, enabling phase reconstruction using noise phase estimates. Oracle experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach under ideal conditions. Evaluations on VB-DMD and WSJ0-CHiME3 show that MSGLA variants match or slightly outperform existing methods, including direct phase estimation and DNN-based sign prediction, particularly in background noise suppression.

items.title: Through-Wall Radar Speech Acquisition via Cascaded Attention Fusion
items.authors: Ruotong Ding(Nanyang Technological University); Zhi-Wei Tan(Nanyang Technological University); V.G. Reju(Cochin University of Science and Technology); Andy W. H. Khong(Nanyang Technological University)
items.abstract: Speech acquisition using through-barrier radar sensing is challenging due to severe band limitation, distortion, and interference. Conventional deep learning models struggle to capture long-range temporal dependencies and recover missing high-frequency components. To address these challenges, we developed the Cascaded Attention Fusion Transformer (CAF-Former), which integrates progressive spectral expansion with a cascaded attention hierarchy. Temporal structure is modeled via multi-query self-attention that diversifies contextual representations while sharing a common basis. The resulting features are fused through a frequency-domain attention module that recalibrates spectral relations and models cross-frequency interactions. This design enables more effective high-frequency recovery and achieves consistent improvements over transformer baselines and state-of-the-art models under severe degradation.

items.title: Ego-Noise-Aware Spatial Filtering for Reliable UAV Audition in Extreme Low-SNR Conditions
items.authors: Chanhong Jeon(Sungkyunkwan University); Jeongmin Lee(Sungkyunkwan University); Hyungjoo Seo(University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Kyuhong Shim(Sungkyunkwan University); Taewook Kang(Sungkyunkwan University)
items.abstract: This paper presents a speech enhancement framework for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) audition systems operating under severe ego-noise. UAV ego-noise exhibits three structural properties: strong temporal correlation, frequency-varying noise composition, and amplitude stationarity, which respectively destabilize direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation, corrupt noise covariance matrix (NCM) estimation, and cause residual ego-noise to persist after beamforming. We utilize these properties to construct a drone-noise-aware speech enhancement system. We obtain reliable DoA via phase-consistency-guided time-frequency (TF) bin selection and use it to parameterize both a crossover-based hybrid NCM estimation and post-filter with a data-driven null direction and variance modulation for suppressing residual noise. Experiments demonstrate 98.12% DoA accuracy at −25dB SNR with consistent SI-SDR and speech quality improvements over baselines across anechoic and reverberant conditions.

items.title: Cross-Modal Consistency-Aware Structured Pruning for Efficient Speech Enhancement with Air- and Bone-Conduction Microphones
items.authors: Yeeun Kim(POSTECH); Yonghun Song(POSTECH); Yunsik Kim(POSTECH); Yoonyoung Chung(POSTECH; Intus Co. Ltd.)
items.abstract: Multimodal speech enhancement (MMSE) improves speech intelligibility in noisy environments by leveraging complementary strengths of various signals. However, complex MMSE models and substantial computational demands pose challenges for implementation on wearable devices. This motivates model compression; however, prior approaches are often not tailored to multimodal fusion and may fail to preserve features critical for fusion under practical noise and cross-modal mismatch. To address these limitations, we introduce cross-modal consistency-aware structured pruning (CCAP). CCAP estimates channel importance using modality-wise zero masking and ranks channels by response consistency with the multimodal input to preserve modality-shared information. Experiments on a paired air/bone microphone dataset show that CCAP improves PESQ and STOI across multiple architectures over prior pruning baselines and reduces inference latency at equivalent pruning ratios, supporting embedded deployment.

items.title: DroFiT: A Lightweight Band-Fused Frequency Attention Toward Real-Time UAV Speech Enhancement
items.authors: Jeongmin Lee(Sungkyunkwan University); Chanhong Jeon(Sungkyunkwan University); Hyungjoo Seo(University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Kyuhong Shim(Sungkyunkwan University); Taewook Kang(Sungkyunkwan University)
items.abstract: This paper proposes DroFiT (Drone Frequency lightweight Transformer), a single-microphone speech enhancement network for severe drone ego-noise. A Full/Sub-band encoder-decoder compresses the noisy input at different ratios, where the sub-band path focuses on low-frequency detail and the full-band path retains global spectral context. A Pre-TCN(Temporal Convolutional Network) captures the harmonic and stationary structure of drone noise and a frequency-wise Transformer attends over the concatenated Full/Sub band tokens, allowing the Full/Sub-band features to complement each other in a shared attention space. The model is evaluated on the VoiceBank-DEMAND dataset mixed with recorded drone noise. Compared to drone-oriented baselines such as DCU-net and SMoLnet-T, DroFiT achieves enhancement performance while reducing computation by 15-26× and 9-15×, respectively. With 168k parameters, it supports incremental(frame-wise streaming) inference and is suitable for resource-constrained UAVs.

items.title: mmWave Radar Aware Dual-Conditioned GAN for Speech Reconstruction of Signals With Low SNR
items.authors: JASH KARANI(Birla Institute of Technology and Science); Adithya Chittem(Birla Institute of Technology and Science); Deepan Roy(Birla Institute of Technology and Science); Sandeep Joshi(Birla Institute of Technology and Science)
items.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar captures are band-limited and noisy, making for difficult reconstruction of intelligible full-bandwidth speech. In this work, we propose a two-stage speech reconstruction pipeline for mmWave using a Radar-Aware Dual-conditioned Generative Adversarial Network (RAD-GAN), which is capable of performing bandwidth extension on signals with low signal-to-noise ratios (-5 dB to -1 dB), captured through glass walls. We propose an mmWave-tailored Multi-Mel Discriminator (MMD) and a Residual Fusion Gate (RFG) to enhance the generator input to process multiple conditioning channels. The proposed two-stage pipeline involves pre-training the model on synthetically clipped clean speech and fine-tuning on fused mel spectrograms generated by the RFG. We empirically show that the proposed method, trained on a limited dataset, with no pre-trained modules, and no data augmentations, outperformed state-of-the-art approaches for this specific task.

items.title: Deep Learning Based Relative Transfer Matrix Estimation for Multiple Sources and Multiple Microphones
items.authors: Oshan A. B. Yalegama(University of Moratuwa); Wageesha N. Manamperi(University of Moratuwa; The Australian National University)
items.abstract: The Relative Transfer Matrix (ReTM), recently introduced as a generalization of the relative transfer function for multiple receivers and sources, shows promising performance when applied to speech enhancement in noisy environments. Estimating the ReTM of sound sources by exploiting the covariance matrices of multichannel recordings is highly beneficial for practical applications and, to date, remains the only proposed approach. This paper investigates deep learning-based ReTM estimation. We propose three novel supervised learning frameworks using time- and short-time frequency transform domain convolutional networks, and a Long Short-Term Memory-based recurrent neural network. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed models achieve more accurate estimation of the ReTM using five objective metrics compared to the covariance-based method. We also show the effectiveness of the proposed frameworks for speech enhancement, achieving performance on par with the baseline method.

items.title: Cloud-Boosted Low-Compute Multi-Channel Speech Enhancement
items.authors: Xulin Fan(University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Juan Azcarreta(Meta Reality Labs Research); Ashutosh Pandey(Meta Reality Labs Research); Jesus Alvarez(Meta Reality Labs Research); Ke Tan(Meta Reality Labs Research); Jacob Donley(Meta Reality Labs Research); Ritwik Giri(Meta Reality Labs Research); Buye Xu(Meta Reality Labs Research)
items.abstract: Low-latency, low-compute speech enhancement is essential for wearable devices with real-time communication requirements, but strict computational constraints significantly limit on-device performance. Knowledge Boosting has been proposed as an effective approach to improve edge model performance by leveraging a more capable server-side model, but performance gains for speech enhancement have been limited. We propose a collaborative framework incorporating three techniques: (1) delayed server output as additional input, (2) layerwise feature boosting that transfers intermediate server representations to guide edge inference, and (3) collaborative multichannel Wiener filtering, which fuses weighted covariance matrices estimated from both server and edge models for improved beamforming. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed collaborative framework significantly outperforms the edge-only baseline with minimal additional computational overhead.

items.title: PolyBench: Benchmarking LLM-based TTS Systems for Chinese Polyphone Disambiguation
items.authors: Chunhui Lu(Samsung R&D Institute China-Beijing); Rui Zhou(Samsung R&D Institute China-Beijing); Feifan Chen(Samsung R&D Institute China-Beijing); Liming Song(Samsung R&D Institute China-Beijing); YoonChoon Hwang(Mobile eXperience Business, Samsung Electronics); Junkwang Oh(Mobile eXperience Business, Samsung Electronics); Gunu Jho(Mobile eXperience Business, Samsung Electronics)
items.abstract: Large Language Model-based Text-to-Speech (LLM-TTS) systems have achieved remarkable progress in speech synthesis. However, evaluating their ability to handle Chinese polyphonic characters remains unexplored. This paper introduces PolyBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating Chinese polyphone disambiguation in LLM-TTS systems. We construct three test sets covering 494 polyphonic characters and 88 polyphonic words across diverse categories. Additionally, we explore automatic pronunciation labeling using Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) and benchmark 17 open source systems. Evaluation results reveal that even the best system achieves only 82.02% pronunciation accuracy on polyphonic characters, with significant performance gaps in dialectal, colloquial, and literary categories, revealing the limitations of current TTS systems in polyphone disambiguation and the need for improvement.

items.title: Towards a Phonology-Informed Evaluation of Multilingual TTS
items.authors: Sneha Ray Barman(IIT Guwahati); Neeraj Kumar Sharma(IIT Guwahati); Shakuntala Mahanta(IIT Guwahati)
items.abstract: Neural TTS systems can sound natural across languages, but naturalness does not guarantee the preservation of sound contrasts that distinguish words from their grammatical forms. Standard metrics like MOS do not test for this. We propose a classifier-based framework that audits TTS output against language-specific phonological patterns using human speech as a benchmark. Testing Assamese advanced tongue root (ATR) vowel harmony with Meta's MMS TTS, we show that a classifier trained on human speech transfers to synthesized speech with minimal loss. The faithfulness audit reveals that [+ATR] mid vowels are realized as [-ATR] in 1/3 tokens despite an underlying [+ATR] specification, a bias absent in human speech. At the word level, predicted ATR labels classify harmony more accurately than transcription labels, indicating a gap between intended and produced phonology. The framework offers task-specific diagnostics and generalizes to other phonological contrasts with measurable acoustic cues.

items.title: An Evaluation Framework for Text-to-Speech Voice Reconstruction
items.authors: Ariadna Sanchez(University of Edinburgh); Christoph Minixhofer(University of Edinburgh); Korin Richmond(University of Edinburgh); Ondřej Klejch(University of Edinburgh); Peter Bell(University of Edinburgh); Simon King(University of Edinburgh)
items.abstract: Voice reconstruction using Text-to-Speech (TTS) offers a communication method for people with speech disorders, which aims to retain their speaker identity while improving intelligibility. Previous work generally relies on Mean Opinion Score (MOS) to evaluate naturalness and speaker similarity, but this has limited sensitivity and reliability. We propose an evaluation framework with subjective and objective components. Subjectively, we evaluate perceived intelligibility and speaker identity using Best Worst Scaling (BWS) with situational framing. Objectively, we demonstrate that standard measures fail to predict reconstruction success for highly unintelligible speakers, so we introduce a novel dual-reference distributional measure to assess the trade-off between intelligibility and speaker identity. By evaluating the output of 17 zero-shot TTS systems for 193 speakers, we show that our framework provides a reliable and task-aligned approach for assessing voice reconstruction.

items.title: Evaluating Automatic Laughter Phone Annotation for Socially-Situated Laughter Synthesis
items.authors: Hiroki Mori(Utsunomiya University); Hiroto Ueda(Utsunomiya University)
items.abstract: Laughter synthesis remains underdeveloped in current conversational agent technologies. Laughter appears in diverse forms reflecting individuality, emotion, and social context. To model this diversity and generating appropriate laughter, annotating laughter phones is crucial, but it involves an immense workload. This study evaluates automatic laughter phone annotation for conversational laughter synthesis. Using a newly annotated eleven-speaker dataset, we built an improved laughter phone recognizer and constructed two laughter synthesizers, a statistical parametric speech synthesis (SPSS)-based model and an audio-LLM-based model, using manual and automatic phone labels. Listening tests showed that the audio-LLM-based synthesizer achieved higher naturalness, whereas the SPSS-based synthesizer achieved higher reproducibility of the way of laughing, and that systems built with automatic labels did not match the performance of those using manual labels.

items.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Grapheme-to-Phoneme Conversion: A Japanese Case Study
items.authors: Tomoki Koriyama(CyberAgent)
items.abstract: Grapheme-to-phoneme (G2P) conversion is essential for controllable and robust text-to-speech, and large language models (LLMs), with broad linguistic knowledge, offer a promising approach. We benchmarked over 30 LLMs on Japanese G2P, comparing them with conventional morphological analyzers on 3000 manually annotated sentences. We evaluated two prompting strategies: a parse mode, where the LLM performs morphological analysis followed by rule-based kana conversion, and a direct mode, where the LLM directly predicts kana readings. The results show that model size, version, and Japanese-specialized training are key factors, with the best LLMs achieving kana character error rate below 0.52% vs. the best conventional tool (1.03%). Parse mode outperforms direct mode for most models, as rule-based post-processing relieves the LLM of handling complex pronunciation rules. We also show that feeding LLM-predicted kana into a kana-input TTS yields better pronunciation than end-to-end TTS.

items.title: The False Resonance: A Critical Examination of Emotion Embedding Similarity for Speech Generation Evaluation
items.authors: Yun-Shao Tsai(National Taiwan University); Yi-Cheng Lin(National Taiwan University); Huang-Cheng Chou(University of Southern California); Tzu-Wen Hsu(Independent Researcher); Yun-Man Hsu(National Taiwan University); Chun Wei Chen(National Taiwan University); Shrikanth Narayanan(University of Southern California); Hung-yi Lee(National Taiwan University)
items.abstract: Objective metrics for emotional expressiveness are vital for speech generation, particularly in expressive synthesis and voice conversion requiring emotional prosody transfer. To quantify this, the field widely relies on emotion similarity between reference and generated samples. This approach computes cosine similarity of embeddings from encoders like emotion2vec, assuming they capture affective cues despite linguistic and speaker variations. We challenge this assumption through controlled adversarial tasks and human alignment tests. Despite high classification accuracy, these latent spaces are unsuitable for zero-shot similarity evaluation. Representational limitations cause linguistic and speaker interference to overshadow emotional features, degrading discriminative ability. Consequently, the metric misaligns with human perception. This acoustic vulnerability reveals it rewards acoustic mimicry over genuine emotional synthesis.

items.title: LLM-Based Multi-Reference Evaluation for Efficient and Robust Assessment of Phrase Break Annotations
items.authors: Younghan Park(NAVER Cloud; Yonsei University); Hoyeon Lee(NAVER Cloud); Hawon Jeong(NAVER Cloud; KAIST AI); Jong-Hwan Kim(NAVER Cloud)
items.abstract: Reliable evaluation of phrase break annotations is crucial, as subtle variations in prosodic boundaries directly affect the clarity and naturalness of speech. However, existing approaches exhibit major limitations: single-reference evaluation assumes a unique gold phrasing for an utterance despite multiple valid phrasings, while human judgment, though flexible, is labor-intensive and unscalable. To address these, we propose LLM-based Multi-Reference Evaluation (LMRE) for phrase break annotations that models the one-to-many nature of prosodic phrasing and generates multiple valid phrasings from minimal demonstrations. On a Korean testbed of 1,356 annotations covering five strategies, LMRE shows stronger alignment with human judgment than single-reference evaluation in both acceptance behavior and score correlation. Our findings demonstrate that LMRE effectively achieves both scalability and multi-reference support, highlighting the potential of LLMs for evaluation in the speech domain.

items.title: Investigating the Relationship between Objective AI-driven Metrics and Subjective MOS for In-the-Wild Speech
items.authors: Jasmer Sanjotra(Indian Institute of Technology Indore); Nagendra Kumar(Indian Institute of Technology Indore); Shekhar Nayak(University of Groningen)
items.abstract: Automated Mean Opinion Score (MOS) predictors are widely used for TTS evaluation but are trained on studio or denoising corpora. Compared to human MOS ratings, O-MOS correlations collapse on in-the-wild (ITW) discrete-token TTS. We conduct a controlled ablation across four systems-continuous clean TTS, discrete ITW TTS (MQTTS), an additive noise control, and ground-truth recordings-and collect 768 human naturalness ratings under a headphone-screened protocol. UT-MOSv2 correlation collapses from r=0.51 (p<0.01) on the continuous clean system to r=-0.01 (n.s.) on the discrete ITW system; other neural predictors also collapse. DNSMOS P.835 penalises an additive noise condition 0.42 points more severely than a generative-artefact condition despite listeners rating both equivalently, directly contradicting human perception. These findings challenge the validity of current objective metrics as standalone proxies for naturalness evaluation of in-the-wild generative TTS.

items.title: SongBench: A Fine-Grained Multi-Aspect Benchmark for Song Quality Assessment
items.authors: Dapeng Wu(Tsinghua University); Shun Lei(Tsinghua University); Wei Tan(Tencent AI Lab); Guangzheng Li(Tencent AI Lab); Yunzhe Wang(Tencent AI Lab); Huaicheng Zhang(Tencent AI Lab); Lishi Zuo(Tencent AI Lab); Zhiyong Wu(Tsinghua University)
items.abstract: Recent advancements in Text-to-Song generation have enabled realistic musical content production, yet existing evaluation benchmarks lack the professional granularity to capture multi-dimensional aesthetic nuances. In this paper, we propose SongBench, a specialized framework for fine-grained song assessment across seven key dimensions: Vocal, Instrument, Melody, Structure, Arrangement, Mixing, and Musicality. Utilizing this framework, we construct an expert-annotated database comprising 11,717 samples from state-of-the-art models, labeled by music professionals. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that SongBench achieves high correlation with expert ratings. By revealing fine-grained performance gaps in current state-of-the-art models, SongBench serves as a diagnostic benchmark to steer the development toward more professional and musically coherent song generation. The evaluation toolkit is available at https://github.com/Tencent/ SongBench.

items.title: GRATS : A Natural Multi-Speed Mandarin Dataset for Speech Time-Scale Modification Benchmarking
items.authors: Ghaida Fathin Aghniya(National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University); Dyah A. M. G. Wisnu(Academia Sinica); Stefano Rini(National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University); Yu Tsao(Academia Sinica)
items.abstract: Despite extensive research on Speech Time-Scale Modification (STSM), evaluation for Mandarin remains limited due to the lack of naturally recorded, multi-speed parallel data. Existing studies rely on English corpora or artificially time-scaled references, which fail to capture rate-dependent prosodic and tonal characteristics. As a tonal language, Mandarin depends on fine-grained pitch-timing coordination, making it sensitive to time-scaling distortions. We introduce GRATS (Granular Rate Adaptation for Temporal Scaling), a naturally recorded parallel multi-speaker Mandarin dataset with 25 speakers and five speaking rates (0.5x, 0.75x, 1.0x, 1.25x, 1.5x), allowing comparison against authentic target-rate recordings. Benchmark results show trade-offs between intelligibility and perceptual quality, and degradation in temporal and pitch consistency under extreme rates, highlighting the importance of tone-aware and alignment-aware evaluation.

items.title: On the Effect of Segmentation Width and Cluster Size on Speech Resynthesis and Continuation in Generative Spoken Language Models
items.authors: Shunsuke Kando(The University of Tokyo); Wataru Nakata(The University of Tokyo); Shinnosuke Takamichi(Keio University; The University of Tokyo); Yusuke Miyao(The University of Tokyo)
items.abstract: Generative Spoken Language Modeling (GSLM) enables text-free speech modeling by training language models (LMs) using discrete speech representations instead of textual transcription. In this paper, we investigate the performance of GSLM on speech synthesis and continuation using discrete speech representations with varying bitrates. We segment speech representations with fixed widths and train K-means models in multiple cluster sizes, resulting in various bitrate settings. We demonstrate that intelligible and natural speech can be synthesized at lower bitrate settings than the baseline. Furthermore, speech continuation quality remains stable at lower bitrates across multiple metrics, suggesting that the conventional GSLM setting may be redundant for effective speech generation. Although LLM-based metrics show higher correlation with human subjective score than conventional metrics, it remains low, highlighting the need for more stable automatic evaluation methods.

items.title: ConformalMOS: Uncertainty-Aware MOS Prediction with Conformal Intervals and Ordinal Modeling
items.authors: Kehinde Elelu(Michigan State University); Joshua E. Siegel(Michigan State University); Mohammadali Saffary(Michigan State University); Tashfain Ahmed(Michigan State University); Simeon Babatunde(Clemson University); Ebuka Okpala(Clemson University)
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of human Mean Opinion Scores (MOS) is crucial for evaluating synthetic speech quality in text-to-speech (TTS) and voice conversion (VC). Most MOS predictors output only point estimates and ignore uncertainty, limiting reliability in model selection and deployment. We propose ConformalMOS, a framework that augments MOS prediction with conformal prediction to produce statistically valid prediction intervals with guaranteed coverage under exchangeability, alongside point estimates. During training, MOS labels are modeled in an ordinal-aware manner by converting one-hot targets into Gaussian-smoothed distributions, preserving score ordering. This improves uncertainty calibration, particularly when softmax confidence is overconfident on out-of-distribution speech. On BVCC datasets, ConformalMOS achieves competitive accuracy (MSE = 0.08) while delivering empirically validated coverage, enhancing reliability for real-world TTS and VC deployment.

title: ASR Under Real-World Constraints: Streaming, Adaptation, and Efficiency
