items.title: A Compact Fully-Open Cache-Aware Streaming Model for Japanese ASR
items.authors: Yinchang Yang(KCGI)
items.abstract: We present a 123M-parameter fully-open cache-aware streaming model for Japanese ASR with a hybrid RNNT/CTC design. To our knowledge, no prior Japanese ASR system simultaneously provides full openness—open weights, data preparation details, code, and logs-together with streaming capability. On a 35K-hour pre-training corpus we show that CER-stratified data curation consistently benefits underrepresented domains but can hurt performance under multi-domain fine-tuning with higher decoder capacity. We further study progressive fine-tuning across five domains totaling 507 hours. Evaluated on five test sets, our model achieves 12.4% average CER (RNNT), outperforming the 1B OWSM-CTC v4 (13.5%) and 619M ReazonSpeech NeMo-v2 (14.1%) while being 5-8× smaller, with an RTFx of 1220 (batch) and 446 (streaming).

items.title: Robust Streaming ASR with Decoupled Separation and Recognition
items.authors: Yufeng Yang(The Ohio State University); Cheng Yu(The Ohio State University); Vahid Ahmadi Kalkhorani(The Ohio State University); DeLiang Wang(The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: Real-time speech transcription that is robust to background noise, room reverberation, and interfering speakers is critical for many real-world automatic speech recognition (ASR) applications. To address these interferences, multi-condition training (MCT) is commonly employed for training an ASR model, but it requires large-scale training data and degrades recognition performance on clean speech. In this work, we propose a decoupled framework that leverages an online speech separation frontend, and a streaming ASR backend trained only on clean speech, for robust streaming ASR. We benchmark the proposed approach on LibriSpeech, CHiME-4, and LibriCSS datasets, and demonstrate that the decoupled framework consistently outperforms the MCT-based baselines for streaming ASR. Our approach is also shown to generalize to large pre-trained speech models, offering a modular approach for robust streaming ASR that avoids task-specific re-training and MCT.

items.title: Margin-Aware Contrastive Regularization for Robust Streaming Keyword Spotting under Strict False-Alarm Constraints
items.authors: Hanwen Zhang(NDS Key Lab, Sichuan; University of Electronic Science and Technology of China); Guosong Zhu(NDS Key Lab, Sichuan; University of Electronic Science and Technology of China); Zhen Qin(NDS Key Lab, Sichuan; University of Electronic Science and Technology of China)
items.abstract: Edge keyword spotting (KWS) in continuous streaming must satisfy strict false-alarm (FA) budgets while maintaining high detection sensitivity. At stringent points (≤ 0.5 FA/h), CE-trained lightweight causal models suffer severe false rejection rate (FRR) degradation against phonetically similar imposters. We propose Margin-Aware Contrastive Regularization (MACR), an offline auxiliary objective that applies intra-class attraction only to target keywords to avoid globally clustering the heterogeneous Unknown category, and enforces margin-based repulsion emphasizing offline-mined hard negatives. On Google Speech Commands V2 under an event-level streaming protocol, MACR achieves > 40% relative FRR reduction over CE at strict points (0.5-0.2 FA/h) with minor changes in closed-set accuracy. As a training-only regularizer, MACR introduces zero additional parameters, MACs, or algorithmic latency to the deployed causal inference graph.

items.title: Mitigating Causality Mismatch with Causal Temporal Relation Distillation for Streaming Keyword Spotting
items.authors: Hanwen Zhang(NDS Key Lab, Sichuan; University of Electronic Science and Technology of China); Guosong Zhu(NDS Key Lab, Sichuan; University of Electronic Science and Technology of China); Zhen Qin(NDS Key Lab, Sichuan; University of Electronic Science and Technology of China)
items.abstract: On-device keyword spotting (KWS) requires strictly causal models for zero-lookahead streaming. Distilling from non-causal teachers introduces causality mismatch: teacher features encode future context. Point-wise regression to these absolute features creates capacity conflicts that severely hinder continuous inference. To mitigate this, we propose Causal Temporal Relation Distillation, transferring intra-sample temporal topology instead of point-wise features. Applying a lower-triangular mask to relation matrices establishes a strictly realizable historical anchor. Our offline bidirectional variant (Ours-Bi) utilizes the teacher's full topology as an auxiliary prior without altering the zero-lookahead inference graph. On Google Speech Commands V2, Ours-Bi improves causal 1D-CNN accuracy from 95.12% to 96.91%. Under a continuous-stream protocol, it halves the False Rejection Rate (8.52% to 4.15% at 1.0 FA/h), demonstrating vastly superior long-context robustness.

items.title: Retention-Preserving Gradient Projection with Entropy-Guided Token-Level Distillation for Rehearsal-Free Continual ASR
items.authors: Seunghee Ma(Sogang University; LOTTE INNOVATE); Junseok Oh(Sogang University); Ji-Hwan Kim(Sogang University)
items.abstract: Large-scale pretrained automatic speech recognition (ASR) models such as Whisper achieve strong generalization but suffer catastrophic forgetting under sequential domain adaptation. We propose a strict rehearsal-free continual learning method that uses distillation from the previous model to define a retention direction. We refine it with entropy-guided token-level distillation, up-weighting confident teacher tokens and down-weighting uncertain ones. When supervised and distillation gradients conflict, we apply retention-preserving gradient projection to attenuate the opposing supervised component with a tunable projection coefficient. Based on Fisher information, we freeze the encoder and adapt only the decoder. Compared with Learning without Forgetting (LwF), our method achieves a 7.2% relative reduction in mean word error rate (WER) after sequential adaptation to LibriSpeech, AMI, TED-LIUM, and SPGISpeech. It reduces the average multilingual degradation on Common Voice by 51.5%.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Continual Learning for Automatic Speech Recognition
items.authors: Steven Vander Eeckt(KU Leuven); Hugo Van hamme(KU Leuven)
items.abstract: Speech foundation models enable strong general-purpose ASR and are attractive for downstream adaptation. However, their size and the catastrophic forgetting induced by sequential fine-tuning demand parameter-efficient and regularized training methods, motivating parameter-efficient continual learning (PECL). While PECL has been widely studied in NLP and vision, it has received less attention in ASR. In this paper, we propose a simple yet effective PECL method based on recent advances in parameter-efficient fine-tuning for ASR. We partition pretrained weight matrices into head and tail subspaces according to singular values and restrict adaptation to approximate rotations within the low-energy tail subspace, preserving dominant components and reducing forgetting. For subsequent tasks, rotations are combined via weight averaging to further improve retention. Experiments on two benchmarks demonstrate reduced forgetting and superior overall performance compared to recent PECL baselines.

items.title: MoDiCoL: A Modular Diagnostic Continual Learning Dataset for Robust Speech Recognition
items.authors: Theresa Pekarek Rosin(University of Hamburg); Matthias Kerzel(University of Hamburg); Stefan Wermter(University of Hamburg)
items.abstract: Modern Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems have made remarkable progress on standard benchmarks, yet performance gaps have emerged under real-world distribution shifts, caused by recording conditions, accents, speech impairments, and noise. Existing datasets and benchmarks typically isolate these factors, which overlooks their co-occurrence in real-world applications. In this paper, we argue that model robustness can be treated as a dynamic capability that continually develops, and we introduce MoDiCoL, a Modular Diagnostic Continual Learning dataset designed for controlled analysis of linguistic content, speaker characteristics, and acoustic environments. Furthermore, we propose a real-world-inspired continual learning curriculum to simulate incremental updates and study how robustness is acquired, transferred, and forgotten. We evaluate three continual learning strategies and provide detailed insights into robustness under evolving conditions.

items.title: SCOLoRA: Similarity Conditioned Signed Orthogonal LoRA for Continual Speaker Adaptation
items.authors: Ye-Eun Ko(Hanyang University); Jae-Hong Lee(Hankuk University of Foreign Studies); Dong-Hyun Kim(Hanyang University); Jin-Seong Choi(Hanyang University); Joon-Hyuk Chang(Hanyang University)
items.abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) is expected to handle speaker and environmental variability, yet deployed systems encounter continual distribution shifts as new speakers arrive. Continual speaker adaptation personalizes one model along a speaker stream without revisiting past data, but sequential updates can cause catastrophic forgetting. Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) offers a parameter efficient mechanism, and orthogonal low-rank adaptation (O-LoRA) reduces interference by separating update subspaces. However, enforcing task agnostic separation can suppress transfer among acoustically similar speakers. We introduce similarity conditioned signed orthogonal LoRA (SCOLoRA), which leverages speaker embedding similarity to dynamically balance subspace alignment and orthogonal separation via signed coefficients. Across ASR benchmarks, SCOLoRA consistently improves new speaker adaptation and reduces forgetting over LoRA-based continual learning baselines.

items.title: Mixture of Phonetic Experts Based Low-Rank Adaptation of Conformer Models for Accented English Speech Recognition
items.authors: Santosh Dahal(Thapathali Campus); Anmol Guragain(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid); Tianchi Liu(National University of Singapore); Luis Fernando D'Haro(Universidad Politécnica de Madrid); Kiran Chandra Dahal(Thapathali Campus)
items.abstract: We present Mixture of Phonetic Experts based Low-Rank Adaptation (MoPE-LoRA), a parameter-efficient adaptation framework for accented English speech recognition. Recent mixture-of-experts approaches typically allocate experts per accent, implicitly treating accent identity as the primary axis of variation. In contrast, we organize adaptation along phonetic categories, motivated by the observation that accent differences are often expressed as systematic distortions of phoneme realization. MoPE-LoRA introduces a fixed set of six low-rank experts aligned with manner-of-articulation classes and performs frame-level routing through a hybrid mechanism that combines phoneme supervision with learned acoustic gating. Because the expert set is shared across accents, the model does not require accent-specific modules and naturally extends to previously unseen accents. Experiments on L2-ARCTIC show that MoPE-LoRA consistently improves over single LoRA and full fine-tuning. In zero-shot evaluation where one accent is held out during training, the proposed method yields a 12.3% relative improvement over single LoRA. These results indicate that phonetic-category-based decomposition offers a scalable and transferable alternative to accent-level adaptation.

items.title: First-to-Spike: An Early-Exit Framework for Rapid and Energy-Efficient Spiking Neural Networks
items.authors: Zheyuan Lin(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Sirui Li(The Chinese University of Hong Kong); Zeyang Song(National University of Singapore); Zhiqi Zhang(Tsinghua University); Siqi Cai(Harbin Institute of Technology); Haizhou Li(The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: Spiking neural networks offer a promising path to energy-efficient AI, yet their potential for low-latency inference often remains unrealized. Existing early-exit SNNs typically rely on extrinsic, non-spiking criteria like confidence thresholds, complicating the model. We revisit this paradigm by demonstrating that SNNs possess an intrinsic early-exit capability. We introduce the First-to-Spike framework, where inference terminates immediately upon the first spike from a competitive output layer. This event-driven mechanism is further accelerated by a Winner-Take-All circuit and optimized by a novel Hybrid Temporal Training objective. Extensive evaluations on speech and neurophysiological datasets show that F2S sets a new state of the art, achieving higher accuracy with significantly reduced latency and energy consumption. Our work validates that the spike itself can serve as a robust and efficient decision signal for real-time applications. Source code is available online.

title: Multimodal Speech Processing and Speech LLM Systems
header: Thursday 1 October 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Area 10 - Poster 1 - Multimodal Speech Processing and Speech LLM Systems

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Speech-Aware LLMs for Timestamp Prediction
items.authors: Vishal Sunder(IBM Research); Samuel Thomas(IBM Research); Xulin Fan(University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign); Brian Kingsbury(IBM Research); George Saon(IBM Research); Avihu Dekel(IBM Research); Luis Lastras(IBM Research)
items.abstract: Word-level timestamps are essential for many speech applications. Existing methods either degrade transcription quality when interleaving timestamps or require separate alignment models that do not integrate into speech LLMs. We propose a parameter efficient framework for speech recognition with timestamps (SRWT) within a single speech LLM. Our approach generates transcriptions in the first step and regenerates them with timestamps in the second, preserving transcription quality. We introduce modular low rank adaptation (LoRA) variants that train only on SRWT data without degrading base model capabilities, enabling isolated adaptation as speech LLMs scale to more tasks. We propose novel activated LoRA (aLoRA) for SRWT, enabling KV-cache reuse thus allowing improved performance through base model usage while preserving modularity. Experiments show a 27ms alignment error in English (35% relative improvement over the best baseline) and 21ms in multilingual data, while maintaining WER identical to the base model. Proposed methods also exhibit strong zero-shot transfer, achieving 37ms error on multilingual data when trained only on English.

items.title: ZEBRA: Zero-Shot Entropy-Regularized Prompt Learning for Base-to-Novel Generalization in Audio-Language Models
items.authors: Asif Hanif(Mohamed Bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI)); Mohammad Yaqub(Mohamed Bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI))
items.abstract: Audio-Language Models (ALMs) achieve strong zero-shot performance by aligning audio with textual class descriptions. Although prompt learning improves accuracy on base classes through few-shot supervised adaptation, we observe a critical trade-off: it often degrades performance on novel classes, sometimes falling below zero-shot accuracy. This exposes a base-to-novel generalization gap in prompt learning for ALMs. To address this issue, we propose ZEBRA (Zero-shot Entropy-Regularized Prompt Learning for Base-to-Novel Generalization), a plug-and-play framework that fuses zero-shot logits with prompt-learning logits, and employs self-entropy regularization to reduce overfitting to base classes. Experiments across multiple audio classification datasets show that ZEBRA consistently improves novel-class performance while maintaining strong base accuracy, significantly reducing the base-to-novel gap compared to standard prompt learning. The code is available at: https://github.com/asif-hanif/zebra.

items.title: MultiEmoVec: Learning Generalised Multimodal Emotion Representation by Momentum Contrast and Multi-task Reconstruction
items.authors: Junchen Liu(University of Auckland); Jesin James(Electrical, Computer and Software Engineering, University of Auckland, New Zealand); Karan Nathwani(India Institute of Technology); Michael Witbrock(Computer Science, University of Auckland, New Zealand)
items.abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition is limited by the difficulty of collecting and labelling large-scale emotional data, as well as the noisy and incomplete modalities commonly observed in emotional databases. To address these issues, we introduce MultiEmoVec, an unsupervised pre-training framework that learns general-purpose multimodal emotion representations via cross-modal reconstructions, contrastive learning, and adaptive loss scaling. Masked reconstruction recovers missing information across modalities, while denoising reconstruction improves robustness to noisy inputs. Cross-modal attention with a transformer encoder integrates features, and momentum contrast learns discriminative representations. After pre-training, the encoder is frozen to extract representations for lightweight classification on multiple databases. Results, including ablation and cross-database evaluations, demonstrate the framework's effectiveness and generalisation ability.

items.title: Unified Audio-Visual Modeling to Recognize Which Face Spoke When and What in Scenarios with On- and Off-Screen Participants
items.authors: Naoki Makishima(NTT, Inc.); Suzuka Yamada(NTT, Inc.); Taiga Yamane(NTT, Inc.); Mana Ihori(NTT, Inc.); Tanaka Tomohiro(NTT, Inc.); Satoshi Suzuki(NTT, Inc.); Shota Orihashi(NTT, Inc.); Ryo Masumura(NTT, Inc.)
items.abstract: We propose an audio-visual modeling method that recognizes which face spoke when and what from videos with or without visible speakers. The conventional method represents information about which face spoke when and what was spoken as a single serialized token sequence and performs autoregressive prediction. However, it assumes that all speakers are always visible in the video, whereas in real-world environments, some speakers may be occluded or outside the camera's view. To handle these cases, we introduce a dedicated token to indicate the absence of a speaker in videos. We compared the proposed method to the conventional method and the combined system that separately estimates when and what is spoken, and which face is speaking. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms both methods when off-screen speakers are included, while achieving almost the same performance as the dedicated conventional method when all speakers are on-screen.

items.title: Speech Recognition on TV Series with Video-Guided Post-ASR Correction
items.authors: Haoyuan Yang(The University of Texas Dallas); Yue Zhang(The University of Texas Dallas); Liqiang Jing(The University of Texas Dallas); John Hansen(The University of Texas Dallas)
items.abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) has achieved remarkable success with deep learning, driving advancements in conversational artificial intelligence, media transcription, and assistive technologies. However, ASR systems still struggle in complex environments such as TV series, where multiple speakers, overlapping speech, domain-specific terminology, and long-range contextual dependencies pose significant challenges to transcription accuracy. Existing approaches fail to explicitly leverage the rich temporal and contextual information available in the video. To address this limitation, we propose a Video-Guided Post-ASR Correction (VPC) framework that uses a Video-Large Multimodal Model (VLMM) to capture video context and refine ASR outputs. Evaluations on a TV-series benchmark show that our method consistently improves transcription accuracy in complex multimedia environments.

items.title: Closing the Speech-Text Gap with Limited Audio for Effective Domain Adaptation in LLM-Based ASR
items.authors: Thibault Bañeras-Roux(Idiap Research Institute); Sergio Burdisso(Idiap Research Institute); Esaú Villatoro-Tello(Idiap Research Institute); Dairazalia Sánchez-Cortés(Idiap Research Institute); Shiran Liu(Idiap Research Institute); Severin Baroudi(Idiap Research Institute; Laboratoire d'Informatique et des Systèmes); Shashi Kumar(Idiap Research Institute; EPFL); Hasindri Watawana(Idiap Research Institute; EPFL); Manjunath K E(Uniphore); Kadri Hacioglu(Uniphore); Petr Motlicek(Idiap Research Institute, BUT); Andreas Stolcke(Uniphore)
items.abstract: Conventional end-to-end automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems rely on paired speech-text data for domain adaptation. Recent LLM-based ASR architectures connect a speech encoder to a large language model via a projection module, enabling adaptation with text-only data. However, this introduces a modality gap, as the LLM is not exposed to the noisy representations produced by the speech projector. We investigate whether small amounts of speech can mitigate this mismatch. We compare three strategies: text-only adaptation, paired speech-text adaptation, and mixed batching (MB), which combines both. Experiments in in-domain and out-of-domain settings show that even limited speech consistently improves performance. Notably, MB using only 10% of the target-domain (less than 4 hours) speech achieves word error rates comparable to, or better than, conventional ASR fine-tuning with the full dataset, indicating that small amounts of speech provide a strong modality-alignment signal.

items.title: Improving Streaming Speaker Diarization for LLM Based Multi-talker Speech Understanding
items.authors: Ju Lin(Meta); Ruizhi Li(Meta); Ruizhe Huang(Meta); Jing Pan(Meta); Xuan Zhang(Meta); Zili Huang(Meta); Jing Zheng(Meta); Ming Sun(Meta); Florian Metze(Meta)
items.abstract: Previous work has shown that source separation with post-processing can help large language models (LLMs) handle multi-talker speech by serving as an external speaker diarization module. However, simple threshold-based approaches lack robustness under diverse acoustic conditions. We propose a two-stage framework comprising a source separation model followed by a statistical classifier (e.g., Gradient Boosting Decision Trees) for speaker tagging. To improve efficiency, we explore a Conformer-based architecture that significantly reduces parameter count. Additionally, to accommodate varying microphone geometries across smart glasses devices, we develop a multi-geometry model enabling a single source separation model to generalize across devices. Experiments on real-world multi-talker recordings demonstrate improvements in both accuracy and efficiency for speech recognition and translation tasks.

title: Speech Benchmarks, Evaluation, and Resources
header: Thursday 1 October 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Area 12 - Poster 4 - Speech Benchmarks, Evaluation, and Resources

items.title: DiscoPhon: Benchmarking the Unsupervised Discovery of Phoneme Inventories With Discrete Speech Units
items.authors: Maxime Poli(PSL University); Manel Khentout(PSL University); Angelo Ortiz Tandazo(PSL University); Ewan Dunbar(University of Toronto); Emmanuel Chemla(PSL University); Emmanuel Dupoux(PSL University)
items.abstract: We introduce DiscoPhon, a multilingual benchmark for evaluating unsupervised phoneme discovery from discrete speech units. DiscoPhon covers 6 dev and 6 test languages, chosen to span a wide range of phonemic contrasts. Given only 10 hours of speech in a previously unseen language, systems must produce discrete units that are mapped to a predefined phoneme inventory, through either a many-to-one or a one-to-one assignment. The resulting sequences are evaluated for unit quality, recognition and segmentation. We provide four pretrained multilingual HuBERT and SpidR baselines, and show that phonemic information is available enough in current models for derived units to correlate well with phonemes, though with variations across languages.

items.title: Tarsila-ASR: A Multi-Domain Test Suite for Benchmarking Brazilian Portuguese Speech Recognition
items.authors: Sidney Leal(Venturus - Centro de Inovação Tecnológica; University of São Paulo (USP)); Ariadne Matos(University of São Paulo (USP)); Edresson Casanova(NVIDIA Corporation); Frederico Gonçalves(Venturus - Centro de Inovação Tecnológica); Renato Moraes Silva(University of São Paulo (USP)); Arnaldo Cândido Jr(São Paulo State University (UNESP)); Sandra Aluísio(Venturus - Centro de Inovação Tecnológica)
items.abstract: Spontaneous speech recognition remains a key challenge for conversational AI, where disfluencies such as fillers, hesitations, and truncations are common. Although recent Transformer-based ASR systems perform well on read speech, their effectiveness under spontaneous Brazilian Portuguese conditions remains limited, partly due to the lack of diverse benchmarks. In this work, we introduce Tarsila ASR, a new benchmark with more than 70 hours of spontaneous speech aggregated from multiple public datasets to better reflect real world conversational variability. Using this benchmark, we systematically evaluate open source ASR models and improve strong baselines through fine tuning on diverse conversational data, achieving new state of the art (SOTA) performance. Our results highlight the importance of domain specific adaptation and provide publicly available resources to support future research on conversational ASR in Brazilian Portuguese.

items.title: Balalaika: Data-Centric, Prosody-Aware Annotation Pipeline for Russian Speech
items.authors: Kirill Borodin(Moscow Technical University of Communications and Informatics; BitmanagerAI); Nikita Vasiliev(Moscow Technical University of Communications and Informatics); Vasiliy Kudryavtsev(Moscow Technical University of Communications and Informatics; BitmanagerAI); Maxim Maslov(Moscow Technical University of Communications and Informatics); Mikhail Gorodnichev(Moscow Technical University of Communications and Informatics); Grach Mkrtchian(Moscow Technical University of Communications and Informatics)
items.abstract: We introduce Balalaika, an open-source, data-centric pipeline for processing audio and producing prosody-aware annotations. It combines semantic VAD for context-preserving segmentation, multi-ASR ensembling with ROVER consensus decoding, while retaining word-level timestamps, followed by automatic quality and speaker-purity filtering. The text is further enriched with punctuation restoration, lexical stress and e/yo normalization, and IPA phonemes. Using Balalaika, we build a 5.1k-hour multi-source Russian corpus with rich annotations, and show consistent gains under equalized training budgets for both speech denoising and TTS; ablations confirm complementary benefits of stress and punctuation and improved synthesis with stricter MOS filtering. The dataset is publicly available at https://hf.co/collections/lab260/balalaika-dataset The full version paper is available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.13563

items.title: Spashta Audio-Bench: Unified ASR and TTS Evaluation Framework across Indian Languages
items.authors: Bikash Dutta(Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur); Siddhant Gahankari(Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur); Abhinav Kumar(Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur); Siddarth Modugu(Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur); Shalini Kapoor(EkStep Foundation); Mayank Vatsa(Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur); Richa Singh(Indian Institute of Technology Jodhpur)
items.abstract: Evaluation of speech systems for Indian languages remains severely fragmented. Models are benchmarked on disjoint datasets with inconsistent preprocessing and metrics, making reproducibility and fair comparison nearly impossible. We address this with Spashta Audio-Bench, a modular, plug-and-play framework analogous to HuggingFace Evaluate, where any model checkpoint or dataset registers through a standardized interface without modifying the core pipeline. Evaluating ten open-source ASR and TTS models across seven corpora spanning 22 Indian languages and Indian-accented English, it reveals what single-dataset, single-metric benchmarking conceals: parameter scaling does not guarantee cross-language robustness, naturalness and intelligibility diverge in TTS, and domain sensitivity persists across all ASR architectures. Crucially, it introduces TTS-ASR degradation as an objective, reproducible intelligibility measure, jointly evaluating naturalness and intelligibility where prior benchmarks assess at most one. We release it as reusable infrastructure to promote standardized, multi-metric speech evaluation for Indian languages.

items.title: Preference-ASR: A Preference-Aware Test Set for Benchmarking ASR in the Era of Speech LLMs
items.authors: Nithin Rao Koluguri(NVIDIA); Sasha Meister(NVIDIA); Nikolay Karpov(NVIDIA); Piotr Żelasko(NVIDIA); Desh Raj(NVIDIA); Jagadeesh Balam(NVIDIA); Boris Ginsburg(NVIDIA)
items.abstract: Popular ASR test sets adopt inconsistent conventions for numbers, disfluencies, entities, and casing, while standard normalizers erase the format distinctions users care about. Current benchmarks therefore cannot measure whether a model follows user preferences for output style. We introduce Preference-ASR, a test set evaluating ASR systems on their ability to follow natural-language preference instructions across four categories: normalization, entities, disfluencies, and case. Built from seven open-source corpora via a two-stage LLM-assisted pipeline with human verification, it is evaluated with a preference-aware normalizer that selectively skips steps matching the active instruction. Benchmarking four models shows rankings shift across preference types, exposing quality differences traditional evaluation obscures. We publicly release the dataset.

items.title: Open ASR Leaderboard: Towards Reproducible and Transparent Multilingual and Long-Form Speech Recognition Evaluation
items.authors: Vaibhav Srivastav(Hugging Face Inc.; OpenAI); Steven Zheng(Hugging Face Inc.); Eric Bezzam(Hugging Face Inc.); Eustache Le Bihan(Hugging Face Inc.); Nithin Rao Koluguri(NVIDIA); Piotr Żelasko(NVIDIA); Somshubra Majumdar(NVIDIA); Adel Moumen(University of Cambridge); Sanchit Gandhi(Mistral AI)
items.abstract: We present the Open ASR Leaderboard, a reproducible benchmarking platform with community contributions from academia and industry. It compares 85+ open-source and proprietary systems across 11 datasets, with English short- and long-form and multilingual short-form tracks. We standardize word error rate (WER) and inverse real-time factor (RTFx) evaluation for consistent accuracy-efficiency comparisons across model architectures and toolkits (e.g., ESPNet, NeMo, SpeechBrain, Transformers). We observe that Conformer-based encoders paired with large language model (LLM)-based decoders achieve the best average WER, while connectionist temporal classification (CTC) and token-and-duration transducer (TDT) decoders offer superior RTFx, making them better suited for long-form and batched processing. All code and dataset loaders are open-sourced to support transparent, extensible evaluation. We present our evaluation methodology to facilitate community-driven benchmarking in ASR and other tasks.

items.title: HALAS: A Human-Annotated Dataset of Hallucinations of Modern ASR Systems
items.authors: Mateusz Barański(AGH University of Krakow); Jan Jasiński(AGH University of Krakow); Julitta Bartolewska(AGH University of Krakow); Marcin Witkowski(AGH University of Krakow); Konrad Kowalczyk(AGH University of Krakow)
items.abstract: End-to-end Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems hallucinate on natural speech, yet existing mitigation methods are typically evaluated on non-speech or artificially corrupted audio. We introduce HALAS, the first human-annotated dataset of naturally occurring hallucinations from seven state-of-the-art ASR models on real unprocessed earnings call recordings. HALAS provides span-level labels, enabling analysis of hallucination patterns and their severity. Our analysis reveals strong cross-model vocabulary overlap and confirms that hallucinations also occur for almost correctly transcribed speech (characterized by a low Word Error Rate). The proposed benchmark with HALAS shows that the character and semantic-level metrics used as a proxy for hallucination detection reach 81% ROC-AUC, while state-of-the-art detection methods achieve an F1 score of only 53.1%. As such, HALAS establishes the first rigorous non-artificial benchmark for the detection and mitigation of ASR hallucinations.

items.title: CSER: Semantic Evaluation of LLM Auto-Repair for Code-Switching ASR
items.authors: Tien Dat Bui(Viettel Group); Duy Le-Tuan Nguyen(Viettel Group); Nhat Minh Le(Viettel Group); Van Hai Do(Thuyloi University)
items.abstract: Code-switching presents significant challenges for ASR systems in voice assistants. While traditional lexical metrics like WER, CER, and PIER measure transcription accuracy, they fail to capture semantic preservation or downstream intent quality in ASR-LLM pipelines. We introduce Code-Switching Semantic Error Rate (CSER), a metric designed to quantify the semantic impact of specific errors—such as language misidentification and minority-language substitution—while evaluating the efficacy of LLM-based auto-repair in recovering intent. Alongside CSER, we present an end-to-end evaluation framework and a multi-condition Vietnamese-English code-switching benchmark. Our experiments across commercial and in-house systems demonstrate that lexical and semantic metrics provide complementary insights, proving that both perspectives are essential for ensuring robust intent preservation at the pipeline level.

title: Post-Training of Speech Foundation Models
header: Thursday 1 October 2026 - 09:00-11:00 - Area 14 - 2 - Special Session - Post-Training of Speech Foundation Models

items.title: Supervised Post-training of Speech Foundation Models for Robust Adaptation in Speech Deepfake Detection
items.authors: Zihan Pan(A*STAR); Sailor Hardik(A*STAR); Jinyang Wu(A*STAR)
items.abstract: Large speech foundation models have shown strong potential for speech deepfake detection, but direct fine-tuning is limited by a mismatch between self-supervised pre-training objectives and spoof-specific artifacts. To address this, we propose a mix-frame post-training strategy to create localized spoof-oriented perturbations and use frame-level supervision to encourage the SSL model to learn local inconsistencies that are critical for robust spoof detection. On ASVspoof5, we achieve state-of-the-art EER 4.50% for a single model without data augmentation. On ASVspoof2021 LA/DF, it further achieves only 0.16% absolute EER gap between LA and DF, indicating strong and balanced robustness across distinct distortion conditions. These results show that supervised post-training provides an effective and practical way to adapt speech foundation models for robust deepfake detection.

items.title: Learning task-specific subspaces via interventional post-training of speech foundation models
items.authors: Jack Cox(University of Sheffield); Jon P Barker(University of Sheffield)
items.abstract: Speech foundation models, pre-trained on large corpora of unlabelled speech data, produce general-purpose representations which are useful across tasks. However, these representations encode information about salient speech variables in a distributed manner, while downstream speech tasks rely on only some of this variability. In this work, we propose a post-training refinement approach using interventional contrastive learning. By leveraging an interventional dataset and multi-part contrastive loss, we learn a transformation from the entangled representation space of speech foundation models into separate content and speaker subspaces. We evaluate the learnt representations on speaker verification and keyword spotting tasks, showing improved out-of-domain speaker verification performance and evidence that speaker and content information are separated across the learned subspaces.

items.title: Learning Multiple Utterance-Level Attribute Representations with a Unified Speech Encoder
items.authors: Maryem Bouziane(LIA - Avignon Université); Salima Mdhaffar(LIA - Avignon Université); Yannick Estève(LIA - Avignon Université)
items.abstract: Speech foundation models trained with self-supervised learning produce generic speech representations that support a wide range of speech processing tasks. When further adapted with supervised learning, these models can achieve strong performance on specific downstream tasks. Recent post-training approaches, such as SAMU-XLSR and SONAR, align speech representations with utterance-level semantic representations, enabling effective multimodal (speech-text) and multilingual applications. While speech foundation models typically learn contextual embeddings at the acoustic frame level, these methods learn representations at the utterance level. In this work, we extend this paradigm to arbitrary utterance-level attributes and propose a unified post-training framework that enables a single speech foundation model to generate multiple types of utterance-level representations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by jointly learning semantic and speaker representations and evaluating them on multilingual speech retrieval and speaker recognition tasks.

items.title: PolyBench: A Benchmark for Compositional Reasoning in Polyphonic Audio
items.authors: Yuanjian Chen(Harbin University of Science and Technology); Yang Xiao(The University of Melbourne); Han Yin(KAIST); Xubo Liu(University of Surrey); Jinjie Huang(Harbin University of Science and Technology); Ting Dang(The University of Melbourne)
items.abstract: Large Audio Language Models (LALMs) are increasingly capable of reasoning over audio. However, existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of reasoning in polyphonic audio, where multiple sound events co-occur and induce compositional structure. In this work, we introduce PolyBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate compositional reasoning in polyphonic audio. PolyBench comprises five evaluation subsets covering counting, classification, detection, concurrency, and duration estimation, requiring reasoning over multiple concurrent events and their relations. Evaluation of state-of-the-art LALMs reveals consistent performance degradation in polyphonic audio, indicating a fundamental bottleneck in current LALMs.

items.title: Step-Audio-R1: Why Audio LLMs Fail at Reasoning — The Trap of Textual Surrogates
items.authors: Yuxin Zhang(Shanghai Jiao Tong Univ.; StepFun); Daijiao Liu(UNSW; StepFun); Haoyang Zhang(NTU; StepFun); Xiangyu Zhang(UNSW; StepFun); Yuxin Li(NTU; StepFun); Fei Tian(StepFun); Yayue Deng(StepFun); Donghang Wu(NTU; StepFun); Jun Chen(StepFun); Liang Zhao(StepFun); Chengyuan Yao(StepFun); Gaolei Li(Shanghai Jiao Tong Univ.); Quanhai Zhang(Shanghai Jiao Tong Univ.); Qiquan Zhang(UNSW); Hexin Liu(NTU); Eng Siong Chng(NTU); Xuerui Yang(StepFun); Xiangyu Zhang(StepFun); Daxin Jiang(StepFun); Gang Yu(StepFun)
items.abstract: Audio language models often perform worse when prompted to reason, unlike text and vision models. We attribute this failure to textual surrogate reasoning: models deliberate over transcript-like abstractions instead of acoustic evidence. We introduce Step-Audio-R1 and Modality-Grounded Reasoning Distillation (MGRD), an iterative framework that uses self-distillation and multimodal reinforcement learning to shift reasoning toward acoustic properties. Across speech, environmental-sound, and music benchmarks, Step-Audio-R1 outperforms Gemini 2.5 Pro and performs comparably to Gemini 3 Pro. Ablations show that acoustically grounded reasoning reverses the usual degradation with longer deliberation. These results demonstrate that test-time reasoning can improve audio intelligence when reasoning chains are anchored to the input modality, providing a path toward multimodal systems that reason across sensory domains.

items.title: Improving Text-to-Audio Instruction Following via Fine-Grained Feedback from Audio-Aware Large Language Models
items.authors: Chun-Yi Kuan(National Taiwan University; Amazon); Siwon Kim(Amazon); Byeonggeun Kim(Amazon); Suyoun Kim(Amazon); Bo-Ru Lu(Amazon); Qingming Tang(Amazon); Ankur Gandhe(Amazon); Hung-yi Lee(National Taiwan University); Chieh-Chi Kao(Amazon); Chao Wang(Amazon)
items.abstract: Recent text-to-audio models generate high-quality audio, but often fail to follow instructions involving multiple sound events and temporal order. This gap arises because existing evaluation and training signals mainly emphasize global similarity or perceptual quality, with limited supervision on instruction-level correctness. We propose an instruction-level framework that uses audio-aware large language models (ALLMs) as fine-grained judges to verify target event presence and temporal relations in generated audio. After validating ALLM judgments on benchmarks and through human verification, we use their feedback to construct preference pairs for direct preference optimization. We further introduce S3Bench, a narrative benchmark for evaluating multi-event temporal instruction following. Experiments show that our method improves event completeness, temporal ordering, and joint instruction-following accuracy across existing benchmarks and S3Bench, while maintaining audio quality.

items.title: CAAD: Contrastive Audio-Aware Distillation for Efficient Speech Language Models
items.authors: Chun Wei Chen(National Taiwan University); Tzu-Quan Lin(National Taiwan University); Ke-Han Lu(National Taiwan University); Wei-Ping Huang(National Taiwan University); Hung-yi Lee(National Taiwan University)
items.abstract: Speech Language Models achieve reasoning capabilities, but are often hindered by massive parameter counts and a tendency to prioritize linguistic priors over acoustic features. While contrastive decoding enhances grounding by contrasting audio-aware and text-only logits, it increases inference latency. We propose Contrastive Audio-Aware Distillation (CAAD), a framework that internalizes the teacher's contrastive reasoning into the student model's weights. To overcome the high computational training overhead in the dual-path token-by-token contrastive distillation process, we introduce a synchronized teacher-forcing strategy. Anchored by unified Pseudo-Ground Truths, this mechanism enables simultaneous full-sequence generation of the teacher's contrastive distributions, allowing student to distill the audio-aware signal efficiently. Overall, CAAD yields a ~8% relative gain over standard knowledge distillation on Dynamic-SUPERB and successfully reduces linguistic bias in MCR-BENCH.

items.title: Distilling LLM Semantic Priors into Encoder-Only Multi-Talker ASR with Talker-Count Routing
items.authors: Hao Shi(SB Intuitions); Yusuke Fujita(SB Intuitions); Roman Koshkin(SB Intuitions); Mengjie Zhao(SB Intuitions); Yuan Gao(SB Intuitions); Lianbo Liu(SB Intuitions); Yui Sudo(SB Intuitions)
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide strong semantic priors that can improve multi-talker automatic speech recognition (MT-ASR), but using an LLM as an autoregressive decoder is computationally expensive and remains fragile under heavy overlap. In this paper, we propose an encoder-only MT-ASR framework that adapts an LLM to multi-talker conditioning and distills its semantic guidance into the encoder during training, while retaining fast CTC-style decoding at inference. Our model employs a post-encoder separator with serialized CTC to produce talker-ordered transcripts, and leverages an adapted LLM-based SOT objective as a multi-talker-aware teacher signal to explicitly regularize mixed-speech representations. To further support variable numbers of talkers, we introduce a Talker-Count Head that predicts the talker count and dynamically selects the appropriate decoding branch. Experiments on LibriMix show that the proposed encoder-only model achieves comparable performance to LLM-based systems in the two-talker condition, while delivering significant improvements in the three-talker condition with significant small RTF.

items.title: TASU2: Controllable CTC Simulation for Alignment and Low-Resource Adaptation of Speech LLMs
items.authors: Jing Peng(Shanghai Jiaotong University); Chenghao Wang(AISpeech); Yi Yang(Shanghai Jiaotong University); Lirong Qian(Shanghai Jiaotong University); Junjie Li(Shanghai Jiaotong University); Yu Xi(Shanghai Jiaotong University); Shuai Wang(Nanjing University, China); Kai Yu(Shanghai Jiaotong University)
items.abstract: Speech LLM post-training increasingly relies on efficient cross-modal alignment and robust low-resource adaptation, yet collecting large-scale audio-text pairs remains costly. Text-only alignment methods such as TASU reduce this burden by simulating CTC posteriors from transcripts, but they provide limited control over uncertainty and error rate, making curriculum design largely heuristic. We propose TASU2, a controllable CTC simulation framework that simulates CTC posterior distributions under a specified WER range, producing text-derived supervision that better matches the acoustic decoding interface. This enables principled post-training curricula that smoothly vary supervision difficulty without TTS. Across multiple source-to-target adaptation settings, TASU2 improves in-domain and out-of-domain recognition over TASU, and consistently outperforms strong baselines including text-only fine-tuning and TTS-based augmentation, while mitigating source-domain performance degradation.

items.title: Adapting Text LLMs to Speech via Multimodal Depth Up-Scaling
items.authors: Kazuki Yano(Tohoku University); Jun Suzuki(Tohoku University); Shinji Watanabe(Tohoku University; Carnegie Mellon University)
items.abstract: Adapting pre-trained text Large Language Models (LLMs) into Speech Language Models (Speech LMs) via continual pre-training on speech data is promising, but often degrades the original text capabilities. We propose Multimodal Depth Up-scaling, an extension of an emerging strategy in continual LLM pre-training, where new transformer layers are inserted into a frozen text LLM and only the added layers are trained on speech data. Experiments with SmolLM2-360M and SmolLM2-1.7B on 48k hours of English Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) data show that depth up-scaling achieves ASR comparable to full fine-tuning while causing far less text degradation than both full fine-tuning and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA). We further show that incorporating E-Branchformer, an architecture designed for speech recognition, as the inserted layers achieves ASR that matches or surpasses full fine-tuning on the larger model while reducing text degradation by over 75% with 60% fewer trainable parameters.

items.title: Localizing and Editing Knowledge in Large Audio-Language Models
items.authors: Sung Kyun Chung(The University of Melbourne); Jiaheng Dong(The University of Melbourne); Qiuchi Hu(The University of Melbourne); Jinuo Sun(The University of Melbourne); Gongping Huang(Wuhan University); Hong Jia(University of Auckland); Ting Dang(The University of Melbourne)
items.abstract: Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) have shown strong performance in speech understanding, making speech a natural interface for accessing factual information. Yet they are trained on static corpora and may encode incorrect facts. Existing model editing methods localize and update facts in textonly LLMs, but do not account for continuous speech representations, or where knowledge is stored across audio encoder or LLM backbone in LALMs. We construct the first audio benchmark for knowledge localization and editing in LALMs and propose a speech-driven locate-then-edit framework. First, we use speech-aware causal tracing to localize layers that support factual retrieval and then apply editing at identified sites. Experiments show that factual knowledge is jointly encoded in layers from audio encoder and language backbone, and that audio editing yield more effective updates than text editing or fine-tuning, enabling fine-grained knowledge control in speech AI systems.

items.title: Towards Fine-Grained Temporal Perception: Post-Training Large Audio-Language Models with Audio-Side Time Prompt
items.authors: Yanfeng Shi(University of Science and Technology of China); Pengfei Cai(University of Science and Technology of China); Jun Liu(University of Science and Technology of China); Qing Gu(University of Science and Technology of China); Nan Jiang(University of Science and Technology of China); Lirong Dai(University of Science and Technology of China); Ian Mcloughlin(Singapore Institute of Technology); Yan Song(University of Science and Technology of China)
items.abstract: Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs) enable general audio understanding and demonstrate remarkable performance across various audio tasks. However, these models still face challenges in temporal perception (e.g., inferring event onset and offset), leading to limited utility in fine-grained scenarios. To address this issue, we propose Audio-Side Time Prompt and leverage Reinforcement Learning (RL) to develop the TimePro-RL framework for fine-grained temporal perception. Specifically, we encode timestamps as embeddings and interleave them within the audio feature sequence as temporal coordinates to prompt the model. Furthermore, we introduce RL following Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) to directly optimize temporal alignment performance. Experiments demonstrate that TimePro-RL achieves significant performance gains across a range of audio temporal tasks, such as audio grounding, sound event detection, and dense audio captioning, validating its robust effectiveness.

items.title: Fast Speech Foundation Model Distillation Using Interleaved Stacking
items.authors: Eungbeom Kim(IPAI); Kyogu Lee(IPAI; AIIS; Seoul National University)
items.abstract: Distilling a large speech foundation model (SFM) into an efficient student model has been successfully applied to low-resource environments. Although distillation reduces inference latency, it requires an additional student model training. However, the training efficiency of SFM distillation remains underexplored. In this work, we explore training acceleration of SFM distillation to speed up model deployment. We examine the potential of stacking, in which the model depth is progressively increased through training until the target model depth is reached. While existing stacking methods improve training speed, they suffer from performance degradation. To handle this limitation, we propose interleaved stacking, a novel stacking method that consistently preserves layer position throughout the stacking process. This property is particularly critical in SFMs, in which each layer encodes distinct layer-specific knowledge. We validate the effectiveness of the proposed method on SUPERB.

items.title: A light weight Continuous Speaker Verification System for Real time Monitoring
items.authors: Nikhil Keetha(Meeami Technologies); Hima Jyothi R(Meeami Technologies); Nivedita Chennupati(Meeami Technologies); Balaji Padmanaban(Meeami Technologies); Harish Rajamani(Meeami Technologies); Naveen Ambati(Meeami Technologies)
items.abstract: Continuous verification of customer identity during telephone interactions is essential to prevent unauthorized access to personal information in medical insurance applications and banking scenarios. We propose a real-time speaker verification system that continuously monitors customer's speech and compares it with an enrolled voice-print to detect speaker changes during an active call. Upon mismatch, the system generates alerts on the agent interface to prevent disclosure of sensitive information. The proposed method uses a two stage architecture with a ReDimNet-B1 backbone and a projection network trained with triplet sampling for robust speaker embedding extraction. Cross-lingual, noise, and reverberation-based data augmentation techniques are used to improve robustness. The system operates in real time with RTF 0.05 and a low computational footprint of 318M MACs. The model achieves an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 2.08% on TidyVoice evaluation dataset, demonstrating strong robustness.

items.title: WaveNorm: A Low-Complexity Time-Domain Neural Adaptive Gain Control for Real-Time Speech Applications
items.authors: Deepika Ijjada(Meeami Technologies); Charan Kumar Reddy B(Meeami Technologies); Ashwini Hanaganti(Meeami Technologies); Priyanka Devrao Jadhav(Meeami Technologies); Varsha Uppalanchi(Meeami Technologies); Nivedita Chennupati(Meeami Technologies); Karunakar Reddy Pucchakayala(Meeami Technologies); Balaji Padmanaban(Meeami Technologies); Harish Rajamani(Meeami Technologies); Naveen Ambati(Meeami Technologies)
items.abstract: We present WaveNorm AGC, a lightweight, low-latency neural Adaptive Gain Control(AGC) system for real-time speech normalization on edge devices. Operating in the time domain, it learns a content-aware, level-invariant gain mapping directly from raw waveforms. Unlike conventional rule-based AGC, it avoids fixed control parameters and hand-crafted envelope tracking, providing stable and responsive gain adjustment. WaveNorm AGC provides robust performance across a wide dynamic range upto -70 dB maintaining loudness compliance with ITU-T P.56 and P.79 standards under noisy conditions, while achieving ~6 dB noise reduction. The model is speaker-independent and highly efficient (49 M MACs, 55 KB of memory), making it suitable for real-time deployment on resource-constrained devices.

items.title: Argmax Pro: Frontier-level Real-time Speech-to-text with Speakers and Custom Vocabulary on Mobile Devices
items.authors: Dylan Angus(Argmax); Chen Cen(Argmax); Berkin Durmus(Argmax); Arda Ibis(Argmax); Brian Keene(Argmax); Andrey Leonov(Argmax); Blaise Munyampirwa(Argmax); Zach Nagengast(Argmax); Arda Okan(Argmax); Atila Orhon(Argmax); Eduardo Pacheco(Argmax)
items.abstract: We introduce Argmax Pro, a unified real-time inference system that orchestrates three state-of-the-art billion-scale transformer models for speech-to-text with speaker diarization and custom vocabulary. The system is optimized to run efficiently on a wide range of mobile devices across iOS and Android without resource contention with other apps and with minimal impact to battery life and thermals. The goal of this system is to offer a peer alternative to cloud-based systems for feature-rich speech recognition with frontier-level accuracy. To achieve this, we built Argmax Pro on top of concurrent research in context biasing and streaming speaker diarization.

items.title: A Human-in-the-Loop Multi-Agent Companion for Real-Time Entity Extraction and SLU-Driven ASR Error Correction
items.authors: Shiva Shankar Arumugam(Observe.ai); Ameyaditya Achar J(Observe.ai); Aashraya Sachdeva(Observe.ai)
items.abstract: Contact-center agents handle thousands of entity-rich voice interactions per day, where a misrecognised customer name, account identifier, or domain term cascades into wrong CRM entries and additional manual rework. We demonstrate MACE (Multi-Agent Companion Environment), a closed-loop architecture in which a real-time companion - an AI overlay that runs alongside the live agent and surfaces extracted named entities as proactive suggestions for in-place confirmation - routes every UI correction back into the ASR stack as either a contextual-biasing entry B or, once recurrent, a post-ASR substitution rule R, with no acoustic retraining and no a-priori entity list. On the English ContextASR-Bench benchmark with Whisper-large-v3, the loop reduces NE-WER by 17.1% and EditRate by 18.6% over a no-biasing baseline, closing 23.6% of the gap to an oracle that is given the entity list in advance.

items.title: Gender differences in the phonetic realization of the checked tone in Kaihui Xiang
items.authors: Yi Zhang(City University of Hong Kong); Aini Li(City University of Hong Kong)
items.abstract: Checked tones in Chinese languages often undergo smoothing, yet their phonetic mechanisms and sociophonetic conditioning remain understudied. This study examines the checked tone (T6) in Kaihui Xiang and tests whether gender differences indicate ongoing de-checking. Using F0, duration, and voice quality, we compare checked and unchecked tones across genders. Results show complete coda loss, but T6 remains distinct through a stable F0 contour and shorter duration. Phonation cues are also reorganized, with laryngealization shifting toward the syllable onset. Male speakers retain a conservative pattern with stronger durational truncation, while female speakers show weaker temporal cues and innovative phonatory dynamics. These patterns suggest Kaihui Xiang is in a late de-checking stage: tonal contrast is phonologized but phonetic grounding continues to shift, with gender asymmetry reflecting a gradual, socially conditioned redistribution of acoustic cues.

items.title: Age-dependent acoustic changes of the frication noise in dental sibilants produced by typically developing Polish children between 5 and 8 years of age
items.authors: Zuzanna Miodońska(Silesian University of Technology); Oliwia Skórzewska(Silesian University of Technology); Natalia Moćko(University of Silesia); Magdalena Krycha(University of Silesia); Michal Krecichwost(Silesian University of Technology)
items.abstract: The paper aims to investigate which acoustic properties of Polish dental fricatives /s, z/ are related to the age and sex of typically developing child speakers between 61 and 96 months of age. We analyzed speech samples collected from 88 children assessed as producing /s, z/ with a target (dental) place of articulation. The analysis comprises a set of typical spectral features and spectral features of the frication noise, which are treated as markers of sibilant articulation patterns. Linear mixed-effect models showed a significant age-related increase of fricative formant distance and spectral energy above 6 kHz for /s/ productions and a decrease in spectral energy below 2,5 kHz for /z/. The results present an age-dependent spectrum shift that may indicate improvement in articulatory precision. The results are a preliminary step in quantifying the acoustic patterns in the sibilant articulation development in typically developing children.

items.title: Age-related Differences in the Perception of Vowel Length Contrast in Northern Vietnamese: The Case of Hoang Van (Bac Ninh) Variety
items.authors: Van Dat Ta(Peking University); Baoya Chen(Peking University)
items.abstract: Vowel length contrasts in Northern Vietnamese are acoustically distinguished by both duration and spectral cues. This study investigated the perception of long and short vowels in this language and possible differences between older and younger listeners. The results show that, at the group level, listeners in both age groups relied primarily on vowel duration, with F1 and F2 serving as secondary cues. At the individual level, a small subset of older listeners relied mainly on F1. Furthermore, acoustically incongruent stimuli (e.g., long-vowel duration integrated with short-vowel quality) elicited significantly longer response times than congruent stimuli, without significant age-related differences. These findings indicate that both duration and spectral cues contribute to the perception of vowel length in Northern Vietnamese, and the reliance on F1 as the primary cue by some older listeners may indicate a possible ongoing sound change.

items.title: Age-related Differences in Acoustic Realization of Aspirated Fricatives in Shaxi Bai
items.authors: Xiaofang Zhang(University of Macau); Infat Lo(University of Macau); Yao Lu(Peking University)
items.abstract: Aspirated fricatives are realized through multiple interacting acoustic parameters rather than a single defining parameter. This study investigates the realization of aspirated fricatives in Shaxi Bai, focusing on three acoustic parameters: initial duration ratio, spectral center of gravity, and H1*–H2*. Acoustic data from 30 speakers across three age groups were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Results show that the relative magnitude of acoustic effects varies across fricative types and age groups. Temporal and spectral measures exhibit robust acoustic differences, whereas phonatory measure shows weaker and less consistent effects. Young speakers show a different covariation pattern among acoustic parameters, consistent with an ongoing reorganization of the aspiration contrast. These findings support a multidimensional account of aspirated fricatives and demonstrate intergenerational change in the relative contribution of temporal, spectral, and phonatory dimensions.

items.title: Listeners' gendered experiences and beliefs affect iconic pitch associations
items.authors: Sasha Calhoun(Victoria University of Wellington); Paul Warren(Victoria University of Wellington); Sara Gilbert(Victoria University of Wellington)
items.abstract: Certain intonational meanings have long been claimed to be iconic. For example, high vs. low voice pitch is physically linked to small vs. large body size, leading to affective meanings like submissiveness vs. dominance. While such associations have a physical basis, we claim they are also socially constructed, affected by language- and individual-specific ideological links, e.g. between dominance and masculinity. We present an experiment pairing a priming task and an Implicit Association Task (IAT) to probe variation in the strength of the pitch~size association. Primes were either strengthening or inhibiting and highlighted the affective link between size and submissiveness/dominance. The priming affected the strength of the pitch~size association as expected; however, the size of the effect differed by the gender of the listener and voice. These findings contribute to our understanding of how iconic meanings develop in speech and the crucial role of social experience and beliefs.

items.title: Age-Related Changes in Mandarin Lexical Tone Production: Acoustic Properties and Tonal Distinctiveness
items.authors: Zhongxuan Mao(Nanjing University of Science and Technology); Yan Feng(Nanjing University of Science and Technology); Chenyu Li(Johns Hopkins University)
items.abstract: Despite growing interest in age-related speech changes, how aging affects the production of lexical tones remains underexplored. This study compared the acoustic properties and the tonal distinctiveness between younger and older speakers. Seventy-eight native Mandarin speakers produced 236 syllables covering all four lexical tones. The results revealed that older speakers exhibited gender-divergent F0 centralization of different tones, contour flattening, greater F0 variability, and longer duration, with these age-related effects varying across tones and genders. Both Bhattacharyya distance and support vector machine classification accuracy showed decreased tonal distinctiveness of the tone system with age. Critically, classification confusion was concentrated on bidirectional T2↔T3 misclassifications. These production patterns paralleled previously reported perceptual difficulties in older adults, supporting the auditory-motor integration model.

items.title: Countering Neural Audio Codec Distortions in Watermarking with Adaptive Restoration
items.authors: Sungho Park(Soongsil University); Thien An Nguyen(Soongsil University); Souhwan Jung(Soongsil University)
items.abstract: Neural audio codecs offer high compression efficiency but introduce structured and non-linear distortions that severely degrade audio watermarks. To address this, we propose an adaptive codec-aware restoration framework that reconstructs codec-distorted spectrograms prior to extraction. Our method employs a ConvNeXt-based U-Net to recover fine-grained spectrogram patterns and introduces a lightweight classifier to dynamically select specialized restoration models for each codec. Experimental results across various neural codecs demonstrate that our model improves bitwise accuracy from near-random levels to over 98% for RVQ-based codecs. Furthermore, by analyzing the impact of quantizer configurations on watermark survivability, we show that our method can effectively improve watermark robustness in modern codec environments.

items.title: DuraMark: Duration-Embedded Watermarking in LLM-based TTS
items.authors: Zhenwei Mou(University of Science and Technology of China); Weili Jiang(Ministry of Public Security); Liping Chen(University of Science and Technology of China); Zhen-Hua Ling(University of Science and Technology of China); Kong Aik Lee(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Kai Gao(Ministry of Public Security); Boyu Zhao(Ministry of Public Security)
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based text-to-speech (TTS) models have achieved remarkable voice cloning capabilities, raising concerns about potential deepfake misuse. Speech watermarking mitigates this by embedding traceable information into generated speech. Mainstream watermarking methods operate at the signal level (waveform or spectrogram), rendering the watermark vulnerable to generative attacks (e.g., neural codec and vocoder). To address this, we propose DuraMark, a robust information-level watermarking framework. It utilizes syllable duration editing to achieve watermark embedding. Specifically, DuraMark integrates a duration-controllable LLM-based TTS model to edit syllable durations during synthesis, coupled with a duration extractor to extract these durations for detection. Experiments demonstrate DuraMark’s superior robustness against generative attacks, significantly outperforming signal-level baselines. Audio samples are available at https://muzw.github.io/duramark_demo/.

items.title: AudioNoisePrints: Model-free audio watermarking using spatial correlation in flow matching TTS
items.authors: Timothy Tin-Long Tse(National Research Council Canada; University of British Columbia); Jian Zhu(University of British Columbia); Aidan Pine(National Research Council Canada); Mengzhe Geng(National Research Council Canada)
items.abstract: We present AudioNoisePrints, a training-free watermarking pipeline for flow matching and diffusion TTS models, which requires minimal extra computation during inference and does not require retraining the TTS model or reducing the generation quality. We exploited the fact that there are strong correlations between the initial Gaussian noises and the generated outputs in diffusion and flow matching models, such that a simple cosine correlation between the initial noise and the generated output can be used to perform watermaking. Moreover, we train a lightweight detector on top for more aggressive augmentations. Our method outperforms AudioSeal, a strong baseline for audio watermarking under strong augmentations. We experimented on F5TTS and other TTS and vocoder models, and concluded that they all exhibit similar spatial correlation properties, suggesting our watermarking scheme can be used for more flow-matching TTS models and even vocoders in the future.

items.title: VoxWatermark: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Audio Watermark Detection under Perturbations
items.authors: Farnaz Sedaghati(University of Tehran); Yuxi Wang(Nanyang Technological University); Zicheng Weng(Nanyang Technological University); Wei Rao(Nanyang Technological University)
items.abstract: With the rapid deployment of speech generation systems in open environments, providing verifiable source attribution and copyright accountability for audio content has become critical. A gap in current research is the lack of a unified benchmark that systematically compares different watermark injection methods under realistic distribution shifts. To address this, we build VoxWatermark by applying 10 watermarking methods (4 neural and 6 traditional) with unified injection and annotation on multilingual, multi-source corpora, and introducing no-box, black-box, and white-box perturbations to simulate real recording and transmission conditions. Based on this benchmark, we propose AudioWMD as a robust baseline detector for large-scale, multi-method, cross-distribution settings. Results show that injection-method diversity and distribution shifts affect detection stability, while validating the effectiveness and scalability of AudioWMD. Dataset and code are publicly available.

items.title: Phoneme-Aware Mamba Watermark: An Active Defense System Against Purified Speech Deepfakes
items.authors: Yanda Shao(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Mengke Zhang(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Zhixin Lin(Beijing Institute of Technology); Tianyi Yang(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications)
items.abstract: With the rapid advancement of Text-to-Speech (TTS) and Voice Conversion (VC), forged speech has reached a highly realistic level, posing serious threats to voice biometrics. Traditional passive detection methods suffer from limited generalization against unseen synthesis models. In this paper, we propose a phoneme-aware active watermarking defense built on the Mamba framework. Leveraging a Dual-column Bidirectional State Space Model, the system captures long-range dependencies and covertly embeds identity bitstrings into speech. To resist diffusion-based purification attacks such as PhonePuRe, we introduce a phoneme-guided embedding mechanism that tightly couples the watermark with speech semantics, ensuring transfer to forged speech during speaker adaptation. Experiments demonstrate effective source tracing with ultra-low latency (about 1 s) and high True Positive Rate under strong purification attacks. Source code is available at https://github.com/Silence-ai423/ phoneme-aware-mamba-watermark.

items.title: The Hidden Cost of Pairwise Verification in Synthetic Speech Source Tracing
items.authors: Anton Firc(Brno University of Technology); Zbyněk Lička(Brno University of Technology); Vojtěch Staněk(Brno University of Technology); Kamil Malinka(Brno University of Technology)
items.abstract: Open-set source tracing is increasingly framed as a verification problem, motivating the use of pairwise metric-learning objectives from biometrics. We thus compare global anchoring and pairwise verification under matched backbones and a fixed data and epoch budget on MLAAD (in-domain) and STOPA (out-of-domain). In our runs, global anchoring yields lower in-domain error (8.61% EER) than pairwise variants (12-15% EER), even with rival mining and XLS-R finetuning. Because pairwise objectives optimize similarity directly, they concentrate variance into fewer embedding directions, reducing resolution among closely related generators. To test if this drives the drop, we impose a similar bottleneck to the globally supervised baseline, yet the baseline remains competitive. Together with an embedding-space analysis (k99), these results suggest that the gap is not explained by dimensionality alone, but rather by the pairwise objective's shaping of the retained directions.

items.title: Teacher-Agnostic Temporal Knowledge Distillation for Resource-Efficient Sound Event Detection
items.authors: Gihun Son(Hanyang University); Pil Moo Byun(Hanyang University); Joon-Hyuk Chang(Hanyang University)
items.abstract: Sound event detection (SED) needs frame-level detection, yet recent work has focused on high-capacity models, leaving resource-efficient SED relatively underexplored. We propose teacher-agnostic temporal knowledge distillation (TAT-KD), a knowledge distillation (KD) framework for SED that distills from any teacher architecture by using teacher logits as a common distillation space. To transfer temporal context, we introduce a conformer-based temporal context projector that models temporal dependencies during projection and a teacher-confidence-aware distillation loss that downweights ambiguous outputs via normalized confidence weights. On the domestic environment sound event detection benchmark, TAT-KD outperformed training from scratch and logit-/feature-based KD, achieving polyphonic sound detection score of 0.574 with 4.548M parameters and 3.668G multiply-accumulate operations, showing competitive performance with far fewer parameters and computations than state-of-the-art models.

items.title: A Sensitivity Analysis of Multi-Event Audio Grounding in Audio LLMs
items.authors: Taehan Lee(Sogang University); Jaehan Jung(Sogang University); Hyukjun Lee(Sogang University)
items.abstract: Audio LLMs have shown a strong ability to understand audio samples, yet their reliability in complex acoustic scenes remains under-explored. Unlike prior work limited to small scale or less controlled query construction, we present a large-scale evaluation of event grounding and false alarms as auditory scene complexity increases. Using 71K AudioCapsV2 clips, we extract normalized (source, attribute) events and build two query types: present-event queries for ground-truth detection and absent-event queries to probe hallucinations, using similarity-filtered negative sampling in an audio-aligned text embedding space. We evaluate four SOTA Audio LLMs with 12 prompt variants over 500K yes/no queries per model. Across models, increasing event count consistently lowers true-positive rate and raises false-positive rate, while prompts induce a strong trade-off between the two. Our confidence analysis shows that models become more uncertain on multi-event audio, revealing room for improvement.

items.title: RAISE: Resolving Ambiguity in Audio Understanding with Imagination and Selective Extraction
items.authors: Yueqian Lin(Duke University); Qinsi Wang(Duke University); Yudong Liu(Duke University); Hancheng Ye(Duke University); Hai Li(Duke University); Yiran Chen(Duke University)
items.abstract: Audio Large Language Models (Audio LLMs) are prone to perceptual hallucination under acoustic interference or fine-grained ambiguity. Robust auditory understanding demands active verification: even state-of-the-art reasoning models hallucinate when forced to decode ambiguous internal representations. We introduce RAISE (Resolving Ambiguity with Imagination and Selective Extraction), a training-free framework that equips Audio LLMs with two cognitively motivated listening strategies. Selective Extraction isolates target signals from noise; Auditory Imagination synthesizes candidate references for comparative reasoning. Instead of relying on ambiguous internal representations, the model grounds every prediction in explicit acoustic evidence. On two challenging benchmarks, MMAR and MMAU, RAISE delivers consistent gains of up to 12.4% without any parameter updates.

items.title: The silence of the weights: a structural pruning strategy for Attention-based audio signal architectures with second-order metrics
items.authors: Andrea Diecidue(Politecnico di Milano); Carlo Alberto Barbano(University of Turin); Piero Fraternali(Politecnico di Milano); Mathieu Fontaine(Institut Polytechnique de Paris); Enzo Tartaglione(Institut Polytechnique de Paris)
items.abstract: Transformer-based models have become the state of the art across multiple domains, from natural language processing to machine listening, enabled by the attention mechanisms. However, the attention layers require a large number of parameters and high-end hardware for both training and inference. We propose a novel channel-pruning technique explicitly targeted at the attention mechanism, decoupling the pruning of each head and the four matrices in the attention block: query, key, value, and output projection matrices, employing a second-order metric to score the network's parameters. We compare our technique against head-pruning strategies and magnitude-driven scoring metrics, investigating the effects of pruning on Audio Spectrogram Transformer (AST) and Whisper. Our results show that even after pruning 50% of the parameters in the attention block, performance is largely preserved. The code is available on GitHub.

items.title: Trajectory Variance: An Unsupervised Measure of Developmental Vocal Plasticity in Birdsong
items.authors: Kanghwi Lee(ETH Zurich; University of Zurich)
items.abstract: How much does a vocalization change over the course of development? We propose trajectory variance, a per-vocalization plasticity score that answers this question without type labels. A displacement model learns to predict age-conditioned shifts in autoencoder latent space; the variance of its predictions across target ages quantifies how much each vocalization would change if produced at different developmental stages. Evaluated on three zebra finches (183K-274K vocalizations, 40-101 days post-hatch), trajectory variance separates learned song syllables from innate calls (Cohen's d = 0.29-0.57, AUC = 0.58-0.67, after controlling for duration), while no nonparametric baseline achieves consistent separation. Trajectory variance also correlates with spectral flatness across all three birds (r = -0.48 to -0.75): more plastic vocalizations tend to have more tonal, structured spectra.

items.title: Beyond Uncertainty and Diversity: Temporal-Spectral Guided Active Learning for Audio
items.authors: Hui Geng(National University of Defense Technology); Tianjiao Wan(National University of Defense Technology); Yi Su(National University of Defense Technology); Qisheng Xu(National University of Defense Technology); Hengzhu Liu(National University of Defense Technology); Kele Xu(National University of Defense Technology)
items.abstract: Active Learning (AL) holds significant potential to reduce annotation costs for audio signal processing tasks under supervised finetuning by strategically selecting informative unlabeled samples for labeling. However, existing AL methods typically rely on general selection criteria such as uncertainty or representativeness, which fail to account for the intricate temporal-spectral structures inherent in audio signals. These structures play a critical role in determining sample informativeness, making direct application of existing AL approaches suboptimal for audio tasks. To address this limitation, we propose a novel AL framework for audio, named Temporal-Spectral Active Learning (TSAL), explicitly bridging the gap between model optimization and audio characteristics. Since temporal-spectral patterns cannot be directly extracted or explicitly defined, TSAL constructs these informative patterns by modeling the soft-loss distribution. Furthermore, it incorporates feature-gradient similarity to guide the selection of unlabeled samples that exhibit these distinctive patterns. Extensive experiments on several audio benchmarks demonstrate that TSAL consistently out-performs state-of-the-art AL methods, significantly improving sampling efficiency and effectiveness under limited annotation budgets, while highlighting the importance of temporal-spectral guidance for advancing audio AL.
